  the record through the new defaulted
  `AuthenticatedOriginalSource::enrolled_service_original` (`EnrolledServiceOriginal`),
  and an enrolled original always answers `NotRetained` to
  `retained_custody`, so it never stands for admitted work. Each schedule
  occurrence then presents a `ServiceCallRequest` to
  `MeerkatMachine::prepare_service_call`.
  `ServiceCallRequest::from_trusted_host` refuses as `MalformedFacts` an
  association that cannot be a service original: one with a controller, a
  represented subject or contributing work, a basis that selects no MCP
  server or checked route target, or a namespace with the reserved
  `meerkat.` prefix. The installed native host
  (`NativeWorkAuthorizationHost::service_call_authorization`, defaulted to
  unavailable) admits the request once, and only when its whole
  association is the enrolled record. It returns a `ServiceCall` (not
  `Clone`, one per occurrence) whose `dispatch` runs the ordinary fenced
  dispatch, Domain-scoped and runless, for MCP server operations only.
  Every operation is prepared from the current enrollment, the operator's
  grant, the connector approval it records and the operation owner, and is
  audited in the runtime store's service-call audit log (next entry). No
  review composition is attached,
  so an operation that needs review is refused, and the connector owner
  still checks the slot's credential at the call. A scoped composition's
  admitted-work owner reaches the record through the new defaulted
  `AdmittedWorkPolicyOwner::enrolled_service_original`; every other owner
  keeps the default, so the seam is unavailable outside scoped
  compositions and on ungoverned machines. The `ServiceOccurrence` a
  request carries is host-asserted audit data, not authority. Additive:
  no wire or contract change.

- `meerkat-runtime`: the service-call audit log, the native owner of a
  governed service call's audit. No input row's commit can hold the
  observations of a call that no input carries, so the machine builds the
  request's sink itself (`ServiceCallRequest::from_trusted_host` takes no
  sink): it stages each observation in process, and the machine's store
  makes them durable with the new `RuntimeStore::append_service_call_audit`.
  Each call's decision and root entry are appended through the fenced
  dispatch's observation barrier (next entry), after the call is prepared
  and staged at its root entry and before any dispatcher code runs; a
  failed append refuses the call with `operation_observation_unavailable`
  and nothing is sent. What the call stages after that (its outcome) is
  appended once it returns; a failure there is reported beside the call's
  result (`ServiceCallOutcome::audit`), and the `ServiceCall` then refuses
  every later call before it is sent; so does a call dropped while one of
  its appends is in the store. An operation whose rows end at its entry,
  with no outcome row, was cancelled or lost after its entry was written:
  its outcome is unknown, as `ToolError::OutcomeUncertain` means for an
  interrupted run's call. A store's append must not wait without bound, since the
  call waits for it before it is sent. Rows are
  `StoredAuthorizationAuditObservation`s keyed by the service original's
  identity digest, the occurrence and a store-assigned sequence
  (`ServiceCallAuditKey`, `ServiceCallRequest::audit_key`), and
  `RuntimeStore::read_service_call_audit` is their protected native read.
  The SQLite and in-memory stores implement both. Every other store, the
  host store SPI's runtime store included, keeps the provided defaults,
  which answer `Unsupported`: it compiles, and refuses every service call
  before it is sent. A decorator forwards both. A machine without a store
  admits no service call. In SQLite the log is its own
  schema domain, `runtime-service-call-audit`, provisioned by the first
  append; a binary without the domain leaves it alone and still opens the
  file.

- `meerkat-core`: `authorization::OperationObservationBarrier` and
  `ToolDispatchContext::with_observation_barrier`. A fenced dispatch whose
  context carries a barrier awaits it after the call's decision is
  prepared, any review admitted and the root entry staged, and before any
  dispatcher code runs, then checks the decision again. A decision
  prepared again during the wait (an owner change) is staged with a new
  root entry and the barrier is awaited once more, at most three times
  before the call is refused as `ReprepareRequired`, so what the barrier
  made durable carries the decision the call enters with. A barrier error
  refuses the call with `operation_observation_unavailable`, unsent. Only
  the native runtime installs one, for a governed service call; a context
  without one is dispatched exactly as before. Additive.

- `meerkat-mob`: `MobLifecycleObservation`, a mob's lifecycle as its
  handles observe it without asking its actor: the last phase the actor
  published and, once the actor has stopped, why (`failure`). Read it with
  `MobHandle::lifecycle_observation` or `MobReadHandle::lifecycle_observation`.

- `meerkat-contracts`: `WireMobLifecycleFailure`, why a listed mob's actor has
  stopped: `cause`, `message`, `code` and `structured_data`, the fields of a
  failed `mob/spawn_many` row.
- `meerkat-mob`: `MobError::DurabilityFailStop { mob_id, cause }`, the record
  a mob actor leaves when it fail-stops because a durable mutation's outcome
  stayed uncertain: `cause` is that mutation's own error (the first one when
  several stayed uncertain). It classifies as the admission close it stands
  for (`AdmissionClosed` with `MobAdmissionCloseReason::DurabilityFailStop`):
  no wire code, wire detail or bridge rejection cause, failure class
  `MobRejected`, spawn-many cause `Internal`. Its structured data has kind
  `mob_durability_fail_stop`, the reason, and the cause's own data under
  `cause_data`. It carries no durable resume hold, even when its cause does:
  the mob needs a restart, not a parked member.
  `MobError::without_shared_lifecycle_wrapper` reads through
  `SharedLifecycleFailure` to the error it shares.

- `meerkat`: `ContinuationOwnerService::submit_for_member_incarnation` and
  `submit_retained_completion_for_member_incarnation`, a submission bound to
  the member's mob incarnation. A new key binds only while the owner's
  current address names that incarnation. A key bound at another
  incarnation is `OwnerRetired` for a stale caller, and replays as before
  for a caller of the current incarnation. A session owner is unchanged.

- `meerkat` re-exports `settle_in_flight_credential_mutations` and
  `CredentialSettlement`: after an unsettled credential commit, an embedding
  host settles its in-flight credential work, then reads the status.
  `meerkat-auth-core` adds `McpOAuthAuthority::stored_credential_status`
  with `McpStoredCredentialPhase` and `McpStoredCredentialStatus`
  (non-exhaustive): one status read of an MCP target's stored credential
  through the use path's own rule.

- Bounded MCP OAuth network stages. Every network stage of an MCP login or
  refresh has a bound: each stage (protected resource metadata,
  authorization-server metadata, account preflight, client registration,
  the code exchange, account evidence, and a refresh's token request and
  subject check) gets 20 s for all of its requests, a start's stages get
  60 s together, and a completion's get 60 s together, never past the
  attempt's own 300 s window. A completion observes its credential commit
  for 60 s. `McpOAuthNetworkBounds` holds these (`MCP_OAUTH_STAGE_BOUND`,
  `MCP_OAUTH_START_BOUND`, `MCP_OAUTH_COMPLETION_BOUND`,
  `MCP_OAUTH_COMMIT_OBSERVATION_BOUND`); an embedding host sets them with
  `HostAuthService::with_mcp_network_bounds` or
  `McpOAuthAuthority::with_network_bounds`, and they hold for the
  authority's own client, a host-supplied one and the account strategy.

- A working directory for stdio MCP servers: `cwd` on a stdio server
  (`mcp.toml`, the realm's `[[tools.mcp_servers]]`, `mcp/add`, profiles, and
  `McpServerConfig::with_cwd` for a Rust host) launches its process in that
  absolute directory, on the trusted-host path and under the host's OS
  process confinement, where it replaces the confinement profile's directory
  and is still checked against the policy (on Linux a directory outside its
  mounts refuses the launch). The value is used exactly as written, never
  expanded or resolved. A relative, empty or NUL-containing `cwd` is refused
  with the typed `McpStdioCwdError` (`McpServerConfig::validate_cwd`) when
  the configuration is loaded, persisted, staged or connected, and so is a
  relative `command` path with a separator while `cwd` is set (checked after
  `${VAR}` expansion; a bare program name or an absolute path is accepted).
  A `cwd` that is missing or not a directory at launch refuses the launch
  before any process exists, with no fallback to another directory. `cwd` is
  part of the server's definition: the stdio launch meaning, the session
  attachment record and every definition comparison include it, so a
  changed `cwd` is launched anew, a resumed attachment to the old definition
  is refused as rebound, and realm service secrets stored for the old
  definition must be stored again. A definition without `cwd` keeps its
  launch meaning and attachment identity unchanged. Mob portable profiles
  refuse a stdio `cwd`, and the adaptive layer decision schema leaves it
  out, so packs built by earlier hosts stay valid.

- `meerkat-runtime`: `DeliveryGenerationReader::read_on_notification`, a
  provided method (it reads by default) that a reader overrides to answer a
  store notification without opening the database, and
  `DeliveryStoreWatch::subscribe_sweeps`, which moves for each of the
  watch's sweeps before its tick does, so an owner reads at every sweep.

- `meerkat`: governed admission of host continuations. On a runtime with a
  native work authorization host a host continuation was always refused.
  `ContinuationOwnerService::submit_host_original` now commits one from its
  namespace owner's record (`HostOriginalRecord::from_owner`), and the
  delivery owner admits it through that owner's `HostOriginalBinder`: the
  binder binds Core's exact continuation input for the owed session (for
  example with `bind_scoped_original`, Core's admission key as its event
  key), native admission decides it as any governed input, and the host's
  custody (`HostOriginalSettlement`) is promoted only on an accepted
  admission. `RetainedJobSource` gains the defaulted `host_original` and
  `host_original_binder`, `ContinuationDeliverySink` gains defaulted governed
  admission methods (both in-tree sinks implement them), and
  `ContinuationHostBindings::host_original_readiness` tells a host at setup
  what the bound composition will do. It is refused
  `NoAdmissibleWorkBinding` for a reserved (`meerkat.`) namespace, retained
  work or a non-host producer on a host original row, steering handling or
  a sink that admits none on a governed runtime, an original its bound
  namespace owner does not hold exactly or whose key it does not bind to the
  row, a binder that does not own it, or a bound input other than Core's
  exact input with its authorization added; and `AuthorityDenied` for the
  binder's or native admission's denial. An unreadable namespace owner, a
  host that has not bound its continuation services yet (readiness
  `Unbound`), a binder that cannot bind yet (a session with no live actor
  waits for its host's own recovery: Core never makes a governed session
  live) and a runtime that is not ready keep it pending, and an admitted row
  is never refused later. An ungoverned runtime admits a host original as any
  continuation. With it: `MeerkatMachine::accept_input_with_completion_and_custody`
  in `meerkat-runtime`, the non-waiting controller pins
  `try_pin_controller_client_for_actor` and
  `try_acquire_live_session_actor_turn_boundary_lease_exact` in
  `meerkat-session`, `ControllerReadinessFailure::TurnBoundaryHeld` in
  `meerkat-core`, and `HostJobSource::new` in `meerkat-mob-mcp` refusing a
  reserved namespace (`HostJobSourceError::ReservedNamespace`, see
  Breaking).

- `meerkat-runtime`: governed admission of peer deliveries. On a runtime
  with a native work authorization host every peer message, request,
  response and supervisor-bridge member delivery was refused. A trusted host
  composition can now install a `PeerIngressBinder` (`input_authority`) on
  the machine with `MeerkatMachine::install_peer_ingress_binder`: once,
  after the native host and before any session registers, refused typed
  otherwise (`PeerIngressBinderInstallRefused`: `Ungoverned`,
  `SessionsRegistered`, `AlreadyInstalled`). Core offers it each delivery
  whose sender the transport established (a signature a listener verified,
  or an in-process sender: `PeerIngressSenderAuthentication` in
  `meerkat-core`, which the comms queue records on each claim) as a
  facts-only `PeerIngressBindRequest`: the receiving session, the origin
  (`PeerIngressOrigin::Comms` or `SupervisorDelivery`), Core's admission key,
  Core's exact input and Core's work id for the delivery. Core admits a
  delivery only as the binder binds it, after the bound-original check that
  host continuations already pass (now `input_authority::check_bound_original`):
  Core's exact input with only the association and the trusted ingress
  observation added, this runtime as the target, a controller lineage and
  model, and an original whose work is Core's work id for this delivery. A
  comms delivery takes one derived input id per delivery; a supervisor
  delivery keeps its payload input id. A denied or malformed binding ends
  the delivery rejected. A binder that is not ready keeps a comms delivery
  queued, and rejects a supervisor delivery with cause `NotReady`, which the
  mob layer or the sender can retry with the same input id (Core adds no
  retry). A plain event, an open-auth listener's claimed sender and an
  exempt route are never offered and keep today's refusal, as does a runtime
  without a binder; an ungoverned runtime is unchanged. A governed input
  whose id names a stored row admitted under another association is refused
  as a replay conflict. A member host reads a tracked delivery by its
  payload input id with the new `MeerkatMachine::tracked_delivery_input_state`,
  and the tracked cancel resolves a payload id the same way: the row with
  that id, kept only when it was admitted under that id as its key (the new
  `StoredInputState::admitted_under_idempotency_key`: the id itself, or a
  governed delivery's qualification of it). So tracked completions and
  cancels reach governed deliveries, and never another input that merely
  carries the id as its key.

- `meerkat-mob`: a controlling host can narrow the operator authority it
  records for a placed member. `SpawnMemberSpec::with_operator_authority_ceiling`
  (and `set_operator_authority_ceiling`, for a `SpawnMemberCustomizer`) sets a
  `MemberOperatorAuthorityCeiling` on a placed spawn. `without_manage()` drops
  manage scope: the member then spawns only the profiles it holds
  (`with_spawn_profiles`), never with a privileged spawn argument (a runtime
  mode, a launch mode or a requested tool access policy), and is refused
  `list_members`, `retire_member` and the other operator tools that need
  manage scope. `without_create()` and `without_mutate()` drop create and
  profile-mutation authority. The lowered facts are recorded with the member,
  so they hold across controlling restarts, and a respawn keeps them unless
  its request (or the spawn customizer) sets a ceiling of its own; a respawn
  whose recorded facts cannot be read is refused before anything is retired.
  A member's own spawns (`spawn_member`, `spawn_many_members`) inherit its
  recorded authority as an upper bound: a ceiling on the child's request, or
  one the spawn customizer sets, can narrow it but never widen it. A flow run
  such a member starts is refused before it starts when the flow would
  provision a member (flow provisions are local, and no ceiling can bound a
  local member); its flows whose roles already have members still run.
  With no ceiling nothing changes: a placed member keeps manage scope over its
  mob, including the privileged spawn arguments, and records the same facts as
  before. A ceiling that narrows the spawn profiles but keeps manage scope, or
  one on a spawn without a placement, is refused with the new
  `MobError::OperatorAuthorityCeilingRefused` (`OperatorAuthorityCeilingRefusal`).
  This is Rust host API only; the JSON-RPC, REST and SDK spawn surfaces are
  unchanged.
- `meerkat`: a restored mob member whose settled build holds mob operator
  authority that the authority recorded with its session did not hold (a
  spawn profile, manage scope, create or profile mutation) now logs one
  warning per restore build. It names the mob, the member, the session and the
  regained facts, and says that a host that narrows a member must narrow every
  build of it, restores included. The recorded authority is unsealed and
  advisory, so the warning is a hint: the build itself is unchanged. It also
  shows once for a profile the mob gained since the member's previous build.

- `meerkat-mob`: `MobSessionService` gains `fork_source_tools`, the visible
  tool names a fork notice compares, read from the set the session task
  publishes at each command and turn boundary, so a source that is in the
  middle of a turn is read without waiting on it. Its default reports the
  tools as not compared: a `MobSessionService` decorator forwards it to
  the service it wraps, as the RPC and CLI services do.

- Supervisor bridge protocol 7 (`meerkat-contracts`), for prompt-context fork
  children on member hosts and for the first-turn report of a placed resume. A
  `Fresh` `MaterializeMember` may carry `prompt_context_fork`, the child's
  fork seed and typed source, which the member host records on the child's
  session and create build; the host-addressed `HostFeatures` asks a member
  host which features it serves beyond its capability report (an open list:
  `prompt_context_fork`), with no effect; and the member-addressed
  `ReadMemberVisibleTools` reads a member session's visible tool names for a
  fork notice. Protocol 7 is decoded but never advertised: capability reports
  still list 2 to 6 and the current and default versions stay 6, so a 0.9.4
  controller still binds, rebinds and reads the status of a member host of
  this release, and either upgrade order works. A controller asks the target
  host with `HostFeatures` before it plans a placed prompt-context fork and
  sends protocol 7 only to a host that lists the feature; a host of 0.9.4 or
  earlier refuses the probe with `UnsupportedProtocolVersion` before reading
  it, and its child gets the prompt prefix. A probe that fails otherwise (no
  answer within 10 seconds, transport, admission) fails the spawn with the new
  `MobError::HostFeaturesProbeFailed`, before anything is recorded; it is
  classified as its cause. A replayed `MaterializeMember` carrying a different
  fork than the recorded build, or a `Fresh` one without it, is refused with
  `SpecDigestMismatch`; a `Resume` of the same tuple (the controller's revival
  of a placed fork child) carries no fork and is answered from the recorded
  build. A fork of a placed source now compares the source's tools, read from
  its member host: a host of 0.9.4 or earlier gives a notice that says
  `member_host_unsupported`, and a read that does not answer within 5 seconds
  one that says `placed_source`. `decode_bridge_command_accepting` decodes a
  command with a smaller version table, as a host of an earlier release does.
  `meerkat-runtime`: `MemberObservationHost` gains `visible_tool_names`, whose
  default answers `Unavailable`.

  A `Resume` `MaterializeMember` may set `report_adopted_first_turn`. The
  member host then reports on the ack whether the session it adopted had
  already started its first turn (`adopted_first_turn`: `owed` or `started`),
  from its recorded build when it answers a retried command. A `Fresh` launch
  that sets it is refused at decode. A host lists the report in its
  `HostFeatures` answer as `adopted_first_turn`; `meerkat-mob` re-exports
  `BridgeAdoptedFirstTurn` and `HOST_FEATURE_ADOPTED_FIRST_TURN` from
  `runtime::bridge_protocol`.

- `meerkat-core`: `interaction::SENDER_TAINT_MARKER`, the line a model reads
  after peer content whose sender declared it tainted.

- Queued prompts kept across a graceful stop. `meerkat-mob`:
  `ShutdownOptions::with_queued_inputs(QueuedInputsOnShutdown::Requeue(max_age))`
  with a `RequeueMaxAge` (default 15 minutes; a bound under one millisecond,
  zero included, or over 24 hours is refused with `ShutdownOptionsError`).
  `meerkat-runtime`: `UnregisterQueuedInputs::Requeue { max_age }` through
  `MeerkatMachine::observe_unregister_session_registration_with_queued_inputs_if_current`
  and `observe_unregister_session_registration_with_queued_inputs_if_use_unchanged`,
  which refuse the same bounds before they start anything
  (`RuntimeDriverError::QueuedInputsRefused` with an
  `UnregisterQueuedInputsError`; `UnregisterQueuedInputs::check` is the one
  rule, and `UnregisterQueuedInputs::MAX_AGE_CAP` the cap). The bound is
  recorded in whole milliseconds and never clamped.
  An input is kept when it is still queued behind the running turn, in the
  queue lane, a prompt, not directed, not bound to an objective, and durable.
  A member's kickoff is bound to its objective, so a requeue Shutdown ends a
  queued kickoff as stopped, exactly as `Stop` does. A kept input stays in the
  session's
  input store with its payload and a stop mark, its completion waiter ends
  with `CompletionWaitError::RequeuedAcrossStop { stopped_at }`
  (`BoundedTurnFailure::RequeuedAcrossStop` for a mob member), and the next
  start runs it once, in admission order, before new work. An input older
  than `max_age`, measured from its admission, when a start finds it still
  queued ends as abandoned with `InputAbandonReason::RequeueExpired` instead
  and never runs (`BoundedTurnFailure::RequeueExpired` for a member; resubmit
  it if it is still wanted). Every start that finds it queued checks again. An admission time ahead of the clock is not
  expired. The generated runtime machine decides each input, and the
  unregister records its disposition durably, so an unregister that a crash
  interrupts converges with the same one. The runtime unregister's default,
  `Stop`, and every stop outside such an unregister end every non-terminal
  input as stopped, as in 0.9.4. The mob Shutdown's default changed (see
  Breaking).

- `meerkat-runtime`, `meerkat-rpc`, `meerkat-rest`, `meerkat-mcp-server`,
  `meerkat`: a completion wait that a graceful mob Shutdown answered by
  keeping its input queued (`CompletionWaitError::RequeuedAcrossStop`) has
  its own generated wait-failure observation, and the generated resolver
  classes it: session not running, reason `requeued_across_stop`, resumable,
  and the surface's pre-admission released. That arm reads no session
  state, so it answers the same after the session is gone, and every surface
  answers from it, never as the internal `completion_authority_unavailable`
  class. JSON-RPC answers `-32003` (session not running) with `data.kind`
  and `data.reason` `requeued_across_stop`, `data.input_id`,
  `data.stopped_at` and `data.resumable`. REST answers `409`
  `SESSION_NOT_RUNNING` with the same `details` (and `session_ref` and
  `session_created`), not a retryable `503`: an unkeyed retry after the
  restart would run the input twice. The MCP server releases the
  attachment's request-local admission, since the next start's attachment
  runs the input, a scheduled delivery re-reads the input's own outcome, as
  for a rolled-back boundary, and the mob host's tracked-turn watcher keeps
  the turn pending. `CompletionWaitError::requeued_stopped_at` reads
  the stop's time, and `meerkat_machine::RuntimeCompletionWaitFailureAuthority`
  is exported. Do not resubmit such an input: after the restart the same
  idempotency key re-attaches to it.

- `meerkat-mob`: `MobError::MemberInputRequeuedAcrossStop` and
  `MobError::MemberInputRequeueExpired` (appended; `MobError` is
  `#[non_exhaustive]`), the answers of a non-bounded member turn whose input a
  graceful Shutdown kept queued, or that the next start ended as older than
  its requeue bound. Delegation, fork relinking and temporary councils read
  both typed outcomes as an end imposed from outside, never as the turn's own
  failure, and the mob host's tracked-turn watcher keeps the turn pending
  for the next start.

- `meerkat`, `meerkat-rpc`: a graceful stop that keeps queued work keeps a
  session's first turn as well. When the stop suspends the run of a first
  turn that is materializing its session (a session created without a
  turn), the staged promotion finishes and the suspension reaches the
  runtime: a suspended run is not a failed first turn. The turn is answered
  `requeued_across_stop` and its run continues once at the session's next
  start, like every other run the stop keeps.
  `should_restore_pending_after_apply_runtime_turn` and its runtime-loop
  variant answer `false` for a suspended run.

- `meerkat-session`, `meerkat-mob`: a mob start after a graceful stop with a
  member's run in flight keeps the run. A host's graceful shutdown leaves the
  mob Stopped and suspends a member's run that has committed a round at its
  last round commit (a requeueing stop), so the run's provisional tail
  outlives the process. The next start restores every member of the stopped
  mob before it admits a command. The store-owned durable-tail recovery
  continues such a run (it keeps the tail and writes nothing), and the
  cold-attach settle reports the recovery's own disposition: when the run
  continues, the start restores the member from the committed snapshot
  under the tail, and the tail stays for the run, which resumes from its last
  round commit when the member's actor is next materialized. The snapshot
  only serves that read; whether the run continues is the recovery's
  decision, never derived from the snapshot. A held, refused or unprovable
  tail still fails the start. New public items:
  `meerkat_session::ColdAttachSettlement` and
  `PersistentSessionService::prepare_cold_attach_reporting`, which returns it
  (`prepare_cold_attach` is unchanged), and
  `MobSessionService::settle_durable_tail_before_cold_start_reporting`, which
  returns `meerkat_mob::ColdStartTailSettlement`. The method's default runs
  the plain settle and reports no continued run, so a session-service wrapper
  around a persistent service should forward it as well: without it, such a
  start fails with `MobError::MemberDurableTailUnprovable`.

- A failed MCP login start says what it left of the attempt it tried to
  admit, so a host can report a clean cleanup exactly.
  `McpOAuthAuthority::login_start_with_admission` and
  `login_start_registered_with_admission`, and
  `HostAuthService::mcp_login_start_with_admission` and
  `mcp_login_start_registered_with_admission`, return what the existing
  starts return; a failure carries the same error beside an
  `OAuthStartAdmission` (`McpOAuthStartFailure`, `HostMcpStartFailure`):
  `NotAdmitted` (this call admitted nothing), `Retired` (it admitted an
  attempt and retired it, durable state included),
  `RetirementUnconfirmed { attempt_ref }` (the attempt could not be proven
  retired; a cancel by that reference retires it) or `Unknown` (a host's
  own flow owner that does not answer). `NotAdmitted` speaks of this call
  only: another attempt for the target can still be pending, such as one
  another start admitted or the one this start would have joined, and a
  status read or a logout answers for those. Every refusal before the flow
  owner's start (account selection, redirect, discovery, preflight, client
  registration, the descriptor checks, a join that fails) is
  `NotAdmitted`. The runtime flow owner probes the attempt's own fresh
  state, never the error kind: `Retired` needs a read of its durable
  snapshot that finds no entry, since a failed write can still have
  committed, and a failed start retries its retirement once before it
  names the attempt. `OAuthFlowAuthority` gains the provided methods
  `start_with_admission` (by default `Unknown`) and
  `retire_unpayloaded_browser_attempts` (by default retiring none), and
  `OAuthFlowRegistry` gains `holds_browser_payload`. The existing methods
  keep their signatures and errors; nothing changes on the wire.

- `meerkat-mob`: `MobError::MemberCustodyDeferred { member_id, session_id,
  restore, cause }`, the typed refusal of an operation on a member whose
  custody restore the mob's start deferred, and `MemberCustodyRestore`
  (`StartupBinding` or `CleanupDelivery`, `#[non_exhaustive]`), the restore
  it names. The operation did nothing to the member's session. The mob
  re-attempts the restore on its own backoff and before each operation on
  that member, so a retry can pass once the cause clears. Its wire code,
  failure class and durable resume hold are the cause's; its structured data
  has kind `mob_member_custody_deferred` with the member, its session, the
  restore, the cause's text and, when the cause has some, the cause's own
  structured data as `cause_data`.

- `meerkat-mob`: `MemberCustodyDeferral` (the deferred restore and the
  `MemberCustodyDeferralCause` its last attempt met: `ServedElsewhere`,
  `HostingUnavailable` or `DurableTailUnprovable`, both `#[non_exhaustive]`)
  and `MobMemberSnapshot::custody_deferred`, which carries it for a member
  whose custody restore the mob's start deferred. `meerkat-contracts` mirrors
  them as `WireMemberCustodyDeferral`, `WireMemberCustodyRestore` and
  `WireMemberCustodyDeferralCause`. The field is advisory and its vocabularies
  may grow: the wire enums read a restore or cause they do not know as
  `Unknown(value)` and write it back unchanged, and the Python, TypeScript
  and Web SDKs surface it as `{"unknown": value}` and ignore a field they do
  not know, instead of failing the read. A `custody_deferred` that is not an
  object, or whose restore or cause is not a string, is still refused.

- `MeerkatMachine::session_input_states` exposes the existing strict input
  witness observation through the selected machine. It includes pending and
  terminal rows, fails on corrupt durable rows, and reads unregistered sessions
  without restoring them. Each row is released as the public row read
  releases it: a scoped run result or callback arguments come out only to the
  reader the input's destination permits. It does not fence ingress or
  establish settlement; hosts must separately establish the close boundary
  and inspect each input's canonical terminal receipt.

- `MeerkatMachine::input_terminal_receipt_observation` proves an input's
  terminal without its outcome. It resolves, loads and natively validates the
  input's terminal-completion batch exactly as `input_terminal_receipt` does,
  and answers an `InputTerminalReceiptObservation`: `Pending`,
  `TerminalWithoutReceipt`, or `Finalized` with an
  `InputTerminalReceiptSummary` (the input, its terminal and attempts, the
  batch's scope, owner and recipients, and the outcome's `CompletionClass`).
  `CompletionOutcome::class` gives the class; one `CallbackPending` class
  covers one pending call or several. The observation carries no run result,
  callback call or failure text, so it answers whatever the reader's
  destination: a host proves a scoped cohort's completion after its
  unregister, where `input_terminal_receipt` keeps refusing the result
  (`ScopedResultWithheld`). Batch corruption, a store that cannot load the
  batch and selector resolution answer as for the receipt. Additive.

- `meerkat-mob`: role-targeted flow runs, so several runs can share one mob
  and one role while each dispatches only to its own members.
  `MobHandle::run_flow_with_role_targets` starts a run with
  `FlowRoleTargets`, which maps each role the flow's steps dispatch to onto
  the existing members that role's steps may use, for example
  `{"reviewer": ["rev-a1", "rev-a2"]}`. Building or decoding the value refuses
  an empty map, a role without members, a role named twice and a member
  listed twice (`FlowRoleTargetsError`). The mob actor admits the binding once,
  before anything is written, provisioned or dispatched: it must bind every
  role the flow's steps use and no other, no quorum may need more members
  than its role binds, and every bound identity must be an Active member of
  the mob that holds the role. A refusal is
  `MobError::FlowRoleTargetsRefused`, whose structured data carries the typed
  `FlowRoleTargetRefusal` as
  `{"kind": "flow_role_targets_refused", "flow_id": ..., "refusal": {"kind": ...}}`
  (`role_not_in_flow`, `role_unbound`, `quorum_exceeds_bound_set`,
  `not_a_member`, `role_mismatch`, `not_active`). The admitted binding is
  fixed for the run and recorded on `MobRun::role_targets`, which flow status
  and run lists return. Every execution of a step, each `repeat_until`
  iteration included, dispatches only to the bound members of its role that
  are still Active and still hold the role. When they can no longer meet the
  step's collection policy, the run fails with the `InsufficientTargets`
  failure class (`MobError::BoundFlowTargetsUnavailable`) before that step
  dispatches any turn, whatever the step's `failure_policy`. A bound run never
  substitutes another member and never waits for one, and no flow member is
  provisioned for it (an installed embedder flow-target barrier still runs
  first, as for every run). Outputs keep their per-member attribution (the
  `StepTargetCompleted` targets and the keys of a multi-target step's
  aggregate output), and a collection policy counts each bound member at most
  once. A bound run cut off by a restart is canceled with
  `ExecutionCustodyLost` like any other run; its binding stays on the record
  and nothing reuses it, so the next run is admitted afresh.

- `meerkat-mob`: `MobHandle::run_flow_with_role_targets_and_external_identity`
  admits a role-targeted flow run under a caller idempotency key in one call.
  The run id is derived from the mob, the flow and the key, so a replay with
  the same activation parameters and role targets returns the same run, in
  flight or ended, without admitting it again. After a restart that is the run
  the recovery canceled with `ExecutionCustodyLost`: it does not run again, so
  a new attempt takes a new key. The same key with other activation parameters
  or other role targets is refused with
  `MobError::FlowRunIdempotencyConflict`, whose structured data is `{"kind":
  "flow_run_idempotency_conflict", "run_id": ..., "flow_id": ...}`, and no
  second run is admitted. A new key admits the binding exactly as
  `run_flow_with_role_targets` does. A key names one run per mob and flow for
  every caller, so callers use keys that are unique to them, for example
  prefixed with a caller id.

- `meerkat-core`: `CoreExecutor::acknowledge_compaction_finalization` and
  `SessionService::acknowledge_runtime_compaction_finalization` adopt the
  runtime's HeadCanonical compaction-outbox finalization (a store-owned,
  metadata-only head commit) on the live actor, and
  `Session::acknowledge_head_canonical_compaction_finalization` rebases the
  actor's metadata baseline over the compaction intents key. Both trait
  methods refuse by default; the store-backed executors and session services
  implement them. `meerkat-session`:
  `SessionAgent::acknowledge_head_canonical_compaction_finalization` (refusing
  by default) and `PersistentSessionService::acknowledge_runtime_compaction_finalization`.
  A `SessionService` wrapper or `CoreExecutor` that forwards the compaction
  reconcile should forward the new method too: otherwise the runtime logs the
  refusal, the live actor is not adopted, and its next checkpoint after such
  a compaction is refused once and resyncs, as before.

- `rkat-rpc`: `turn/start`, `session/create` (for its first turn) and
  `mob/turn_start` take `session_events`. With `false`, the turn's events are
  not written as `session/event` notifications; absent or `true` keeps them.
  A caller that reads the turn's events from a `session/stream_open`
  subscription, or reads only the run result, sends it so each event reaches
  it once. A turn that also carries the input of a request that wants the
  events still writes them, and turns that no turn-starting request admitted
  (external events, comms, schedules, resumed runs) are unchanged. A server
  before 0.9.5 refuses the field on `turn/start` and `mob/turn_start` and
  ignores it on `session/create`.

- `meerkat-session`: reads of a session whose durable run holds a round
  commit. From a run's first tool round until its boundary commit, or until a
  restart resumes it, the store keeps the round as the run's provisional tail
  ahead of the committed snapshot. Readers of the committed session serve that
  snapshot at once, and never decide anything about the tail from it:
  - `PersistentSessionService::load_committed_session_tolerating_tail` keeps
    the committed read's contract (the same transcript rewrite replay, audit
    verification and counted retry budget). Under the session's own applied
    tail it serves the boundary's snapshot instead of refusing with a
    transcript revision conflict; with no provisional tail applied the
    conflict stands. `PersistentSessionService::observe_authoritative_session_body_tolerating_tail`
    is its read-only sibling: it never writes and never replays the rewrite
    audit.
  - Through them, while a round commit stands: session history, transcript
    revisions, instruction activation records, `read` with no live actor, the
    durable body behind planned-fork verification and mob execution evidence,
    tool application observations, a mob member's status view, a member's
    auth binding read, a fork's inheritance read, the fork-off re-link's
    reads, the schedule hosts' metadata reads, and the surfaces' session reads
    and controls (RPC `turn/start`, `turn/interrupt` and `turn/stop_run`; REST
    run stop, `POST /sessions/{id}/messages`, the external-events and
    peer-response-terminal webhooks, `GET /sessions/{id}/events` and live MCP
    add, remove and reload; the MCP server's `meerkat_resume` and MCP
    operations; `rkat session show`). A turn sent to a running session is
    queued behind the run.
  - Live checks read no committed body: the live-session staleness judgement,
    the live presence checks, a live bridge's durable-source check and the
    runtime-backed executor's session check after its actor is gone. The live
    actor of an open run is not stale, and a host restarted over a tail takes
    its cold path, where recovery decides the tail. Live mutations (tool
    filter, MCP intents, mob authority context, tool application) check the
    archive without reading the session, and land after the run. A read of a
    hosted session whose turn stopped before its boundary commit settles the
    tail that turn left, as a restart would.

- `meerkat-mob`: `MobSessionService::load_persisted_session_tolerating_tail`,
  the same read for mob code. Its default is the strict
  `load_persisted_session`; the persistent session service overrides it. A
  wrapper over another `MobSessionService` must forward it (see Upgrade
  notes).

- `meerkat-session`: `PersistentSessionService::live_actor_continues_open_run_tail`
  answers whether the live actor continues the store's standing provisional
  tail of a run the runtime holds open: the actor's latest run checkpoint
  receipt is exactly the store's tail authority, and the run is the
  runtime's current run or the run its registration keeps resumable. Such an
  actor is not stale.

- `meerkat-rpc`, `meerkat-mob`, `meerkat-mob-mcp`, `meerkat-runtime`,
  `meerkat`: a mob member's live channel opens over WebRTC through its mob.
  `mob/member_live_open` with `transport: "webrtc"` runs the mob's member
  checks (not retiring, in cleanup or revoke, and restored), then the
  member's own live host serves it: the result is a WebRTC bootstrap whose
  offer `live/webrtc/answer` answers on the same JSON-RPC server. A host that
  serves no WebRTC refuses it typed (`LiveTransportUnsupported`) before it
  connects a provider. The optional `execution_identity` (for gpt-live-1,
  `{"version": "v1", "profile_id": "openai.gpt-live-1.client-context.v1"}`)
  opens the member's channel through the server's execution-identity
  authority, the one behind the strict `live/open`: the connection keeps the
  channel's playback custody and answers its offer, and
  `mob/member_live_close` closes the channel through that authority. Rust
  embedders get `MobHandle::member_live_open_with_execution_identity`,
  `MobMcpState::mob_member_live_open_with_execution_identity`,
  `MemberLiveHost::open_with_execution_identity` (by default a typed
  `Unavailable` refusal), `MemberLiveHost::close_explicit` (the mob's own
  closes; by default `close`), `MemberLiveExecutionOpen` and
  `ServiceMemberLiveHost::with_execution_identity_authority`. The Python
  (`execution_identity=`) and TypeScript (`executionIdentity`) member live
  helpers take the selector too.

### Changed

- `meerkat`: a GPT Live close (a session channel's `live/close` or a member
  channel's `mob/member_live_close`) whose provider never confirms now
  retires the transport locally after 10 s instead of 15 s: the public
  `meerkat::experimental_gpt_live::LIVE_CLOSE_CONFIRMATION_BOUND` (public
  since v0.9.4) is now 10 s, down from 15 s. A gpt-live-1 member channel's
  `mob/member_live_close` therefore converges inside the mob's 15 s member
  live close timeout instead of timing out on its first request.

- `meerkat-core`, `meerkat-session`, `meerkat-runtime`: stopping a durable
  run (for example with `MeerkatMachine::stop_run`) keeps the rounds it has
  already committed in the transcript, closed as an interrupted run with a
  notice, and the stopped input is not run again; a steer that joined a round
  the stop cut short is not kept. The next turn's model request carries that
  committed history. In 0.9.4 the next turn's request carried nothing of a
  stopped turn.

- `meerkat-session`: materializing a durable session whose durable-tail
  recovery held or refused its tail now answers the typed
  `SessionError::DurableTailHeldForRecovery` or
  `SessionError::DurableTailRecoveryRefused` instead of an internal error, so
  a caller can tell a session withheld for reconciliation from a fault. The
  tail and every durable row are kept, as before.
- `meerkat-session`: `PersistentSessionService::load_authoritative_session`
  may settle a provisional tail an observation deferred while a runtime loop
  lap held the session's turn-finalization boundary, also after the live
  actor is gone, waiting up to one second for that boundary. Its counted
  retries still add no wait on the boundary, and every other conflict
  surfaces unchanged; a caller that holds the boundary itself waits out the
  second and gets the conflict.
- `meerkat-session`: `PersistentSessionService::prepare_cold_attach` (and
  `prepare_cold_attach_reporting`) settle a provisional tail only between
  runtime loop laps. Once a tail stands they wait up to one second for the
  session's turn-finalization boundary, which a lap holds from its top
  through its run, and a lap that holds it longer leaves the tail for a later
  settle; the caller's committed read then refuses, as for any unresolved
  tail. A lap can outlive the live actor, and a settle inside the lap's
  staging window would be written over by its staging commit, which ends the
  input the settle consumed as stopped. A caller that holds the boundary
  itself (a runtime loop lap's apply) uses the new
  `prepare_cold_attach_under_runtime_turn_boundary`.
- `meerkat-session`, `meerkat-mob`: the other entries into the same
  durable-tail recovery also settle a provisional tail only between runtime
  loop laps: `PersistentSessionService::prepare_committed_boundary_resume`
  (and so the persistent `MobSessionService::materialize_session_resume_verdict`),
  `PersistentSessionService::recover_committed_boundary`, and a create that
  resumes a durable session without holding the session's
  turn-finalization boundary. Once a tail stands they wait up to one second
  for that boundary, and a lap that holds it longer refuses them with
  `SessionError::Busy`, leaving the tail and every row as they were. A
  caller that holds the boundary itself uses the new
  `prepare_committed_boundary_resume_under_runtime_turn_boundary`, or the
  new provided method
  `MobSessionService::materialize_session_resume_verdict_under_runtime_turn_boundary`,
  which a wrapper around a persistent service should forward.
- `meerkat-core`, `meerkat-session`, `meerkat-runtime`: a HeadCanonical run's
  round commits (see Added, per-round commits) move its durable head over the
  run's compaction rewrites, and the run retires its compaction history to
  `history_retained_rewrites` after each of them (see Fixed). A host that stops
  after such a commit and before the run's boundary commit (a crash, a forced
  kill, an out-of-memory kill) keeps the run's content up to that commit: the
  run continues from it on resume, or, when its inputs were already settled,
  recovery commits it as interrupted with the typed recovery notice and its
  input is not run again. Before, such a stop lost the run's progress back to
  the committed boundary. Runs without a checkpointer and live bridge runs that
  commit nothing take no round commit.

- `meerkat-core`: the `FORK_INSTRUCTION_REFUSED` message for a fork the
  policy refuses (cause `policy_refuses`) names the setting that changes it:
  "to carry them into the child, set the host's fork_instruction_policy
  (inherited_instructions on a session fork call) to reactivate_inherited".
  It said only that `reactivate_inherited` carries them into the child. The
  cause, the keys and the error code are unchanged.
- RPC: an input idempotency conflict carries `data.code`
  `INPUT_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT` beside `data.existing_id`. REST: the
  external-events route answers it with `409` and the same code; it was a
  `500`. The browser runtime refuses unknown member-send option fields, so a
  key it cannot keep is refused, never dropped.
- `meerkat-core`: the shipped config template's commented
  `[[model_fallback.chain]]` example names a placeholder model
  (`model = "<model-id>"`) instead of a real model id.

- `meerkat-store`: the refusal of a runtime commit over a session saved whole
  outside the runtime, by a pre-0.9 build or by a non-runtime service sharing a
  realm's SQLite session store, names that cause and that a runtime-backed host
  cannot adopt such a session. It said only "legacy whole-blob session exists
  without a canonical head". The session's data stays intact, and the error
  variant is unchanged.

- OpenAI Responses on the public OpenAI API keeps a hosted web search's
  evidence from one stateless step to the next (`store: false`, the
  default). A request with the hosted `web_search` tool now also asks for
  the sources each search consulted (`include` gains
  `web_search_call.action.sources`), and later steps replay the search call
  with those sources and the answer's `url_citation` annotations on its text
  instead of `annotations: []`. Only citations whose range fits the replayed
  text go back, and only for an answer whose text came from one text part:
  the citations block of an OpenAI answer (its `message_annotations` server
  content) now also records how many `output_text` parts the answer had
  (`text_parts`), and an answer from several parts, or one recorded before
  this change, replays none. The text of the pages never comes back; for
  that, opt in to `store: true` (stored continuation) or use the Meerkat
  `web_search` fallback tool. The ChatGPT backend, Azure OpenAI and GitHub
  Copilot Responses wires keep their request shape: no sources asked for or
  replayed, and `annotations: []`. No API change.

- Python and TypeScript SDKs: calls that do not stream their turn
  (`create_session` / `createSession`, a session's `turn`, and
  `mob_turn_start` / `mobTurnStart`) send `session_events: false` to a server
  whose contract is 0.9.5 or later. The server then writes each of the turn's
  events once, on a subscription if one is open, instead of also writing a
  `session/event` copy that the SDK parsed and dropped. Streaming calls are
  unchanged.

- `meerkat-mob`: a keyed flow run admission whose key already names a run
  with other activation parameters is refused with the typed
  `MobError::FlowRunIdempotencyConflict` instead of an internal error, for
  every keyed admission. A schedule delivery that meets such a key conflict
  records it as `MobRejected` instead of an internal error.

- A `turn/start` or an external event that arrives while a durable run is
  under way, after the run's first round commit, is admitted and queued at
  once instead of waiting outside admission until the run ends. Its input is
  durable earlier and still runs after the run. At a graceful stop the input
  is kept and requeued with the session's work, and the request ends as
  `requeued_across_stop` instead of being refused as `runtime_shutting_down`.
  Before the run's first round commit such a request still waits, as in
  0.9.4.

### Fixed

- `meerkat-core`: a peer lifecycle notice (such as a mob kickoff status) no
  longer tells the model there is nothing to answer. It still forbids a peer
  reply (no `send_response` or `send_message`) and now asks for a short,
  nonempty final response for the local turn, so the notice no longer
  contradicts a turn that requires a visible completion.

- `meerkat-mob`: a Running mob whose member's runtime was stopped after the
  restart rebuilt the member, and before the mob restored it, starts and
  serves the member instead of stopping. The stopped runtime keeps its
  registration until it is unregistered, and the restore refused it, so the
  whole mob entered Stopped. The restore now takes such a registration over
  once (after a stop cleanup still running finishes; it waits for one within
  a bound, past which the restore goes on as before),
  revives the member right after the start, and runs the member's readiness
  then, its host loop included for an autonomous member. A member whose
  revival fails is recorded Broken with the reason; any other registration a
  restore cannot use is refused as before. Two revivals of one member asked
  for at the same time (a member turn, `MobHandle::ensure_member_live`, the
  start's own) now share one materialization instead of racing. A member
  whose runtime registration needs a durability reload when the mob starts
  no longer stops the mob either: it is left out of the start, its
  registration is reloaded right after the start (the same reload
  `MobHandle::reload_member_registration` runs, so a delivery to it waits
  behind the reload or is refused `MemberReloadRequired`), and it is
  recorded Broken with the reason if the reload fails.

- `meerkat-runtime`: a public input row released to a reader its scoped
  destination does not permit (`SessionServiceRuntimeExt::input_state` and
  the idempotency-key reads) no longer carries a directed batch's finalized
  terminal event. A directed (peer-request) batch's owner row keeps that
  `InteractionComplete` or `InteractionCallbackPending` event, with the run's
  result or callback arguments, from finalization until its publication
  succeeds, and for as long as a failing publication is retried. The
  withholding cleared the result on the terminal completion but left the
  event (`crates/meerkat-runtime/src/input_state.rs:666` and `:1278` at
  v0.9.4).

- `meerkat-runtime`: such a released row no longer carries the digests
  derived from the withheld payload: an unsalted SHA-256 let a reader confirm
  a low-entropy result by guessing it. On every row the destination does not
  permit, a peer recipient's included (it binds the batch's payload by
  digest without holding it), the terminal completion's candidate and receipt
  digests and a directed outbox's candidate, event and publication digests
  read `withheld`, and the copy is marked in process only: a released copy
  written out and read back fails validation, and a stored row never carries
  the value. Before, only a row holding the payload was withheld at all
  (`crates/meerkat-runtime/src/meerkat_machine/scoped_context.rs:277`, and
  the digests at `crates/meerkat-runtime/src/input_state.rs:424`, `:446`,
  `:650`, `:667` and `:732`, at v0.9.4). On a released copy,
  `StoredInputState::published_directed_terminal_binding` decides from the
  outbox's identity and phase alone, so it still answers.

- `meerkat-mob`, `meerkat-rpc`, `meerkat-rest`: identity adoption refuses a
  mob whose runtime has no store. Reconciliation realizes an adoption by
  retiring the attached member and resuming its exact session from the
  lifecycle record in the runtime's store, which a store-less runtime does
  not keep. On such a runtime (`MeerkatMachine::ephemeral()`, the runtime of
  every mob on an `EphemeralSessionService`) the member was retired and the
  identity then stayed `RepairBlocked`: the member was gone for the rest of
  the process. `adopt_member_identity_declaration` now refuses such a mob
  before anything is recorded, with
  `MobError::IdentityAdoptionRequiresPersistentRuntime`
  (`CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE`: `-32020` over JSON-RPC, HTTP 501 over REST;
  `data.kind` `mob_identity_adoption_requires_persistent_runtime`), and the
  member stays attached and serving. Build the mob over the persistent
  session service to adopt its members: a mob in any realm, `memory`
  included, can.

- `meerkat-session`, `meerkat-runtime`, `meerkat-rest`, `meerkat-mcp-server`:
  a start or attach of a HeadCanonical session whose durable tail its
  recovery withholds from resume (held for recovery or refused by recovery)
  now refuses with that typed hold (`SESSION_DURABLE_TAIL_HELD_FOR_RECOVERY`
  or `SESSION_DURABLE_TAIL_RECOVERY_REFUSED`, with the `durable_resume_hold`
  payload) before it reads the session.
  `PersistentSessionService::prepare_cold_attach` logged the hold and let the
  caller's committed read meet the tail, so a JSON-RPC `turn/start` answered
  `SESSION_STORE_ERROR` ("rewrite rejected: previous transcript revision ...
  did not match commit parent"), REST `500`, and the MCP server's
  `meerkat_resume` an internal error (shipped in 0.9.4:
  `crates/meerkat-session/src/persistent.rs:16504-16510` at v0.9.4). Nothing
  is written: the tail and the session's inputs stay for reconciliation.
  JSON-RPC and the MCP server answer the canonical `SESSION_NOT_RUNNING`
  form (JSON-RPC `-32003`) with the hold's `durable_resume_hold` payload,
  whose `session_error_code` names the hold; REST carries the hold through
  its attach path as the new `RuntimeDriverError::DurableResumeHeld` (an
  additive variant of the `#[non_exhaustive]` enum, with
  `durable_hold_session_error()`) and answers `409` `SESSION_NOT_RUNNING`
  with the same payload. `DurableResumeHold::session_error` builds the typed
  error from a hold. A mob member restore answers
  `MemberDurableTailUnprovable`, as for a tail its recovery could not prove.

- `meerkat-rest`: an archive refused with a durable resume hold answers `409`
  `SESSION_NOT_RUNNING` with the hold's `durable_resume_hold` payload (its
  `session_error_code` names the hold) instead of an internal `500`. In
  0.9.4 an archive of a WholeBlob session whose document needs the
  audited-endpoint repair met this: the archive's committed read refused
  with `WholeBlobAuditedEndpointDivergence`
  (`crates/meerkat-session/src/persistent.rs:14377` and `128-139` at
  v0.9.4), and `archive_session_error_to_api_error` answered it `Internal`
  (`crates/meerkat-rest/src/lib.rs:6560-6578` at v0.9.4).

- `meerkat-runtime`, `meerkat-machine-schema`, `meerkat-machine-kernels`: a
  session that completes more than 256 inputs at once no longer becomes
  reload-required. One terminal-completion batch names at most 256 inputs:
  its owner row carries the whole recipient set, every released reader
  validates the bound at load, and its finalization and receipt writes are
  one input-state batch CAS (`MAX_INPUT_STATE_BATCH_CAS`). A run took every
  queued input of a compatible lane, and a stop, destroy, retire, retirement
  cleanup, attachment replacement or reset completed every active input as
  one batch, so a backlog past 256 was refused after the terminal checkpoint,
  which marks the registration reload-required (a mob member with a large
  backlog could stop its whole mob). A run now stages at most 256 inputs
  (`command_capabilities::RUNTIME_LOOP_BATCH_MAX_INPUTS`) and the rest of its
  lane runs in the next run, in admission order. A runless termination
  completes every input in batches of at most 256, committed together in its
  one durable commit. Past 256 contributors (a run's batch and its joins; a
  resumed run's batch includes the inputs its committed rounds already
  applied), a durable Steer that cannot join the running turn is delivered in
  the next run instead: the machine's `JoinLiveBoundaryDurableAppend` gains
  the `run_contributor_capacity` guard. A recipient set past the bound is
  refused, typed, before any checkpoint.

- `meerkat-runtime`: a retire no longer hangs when its runtime loop has many
  wakes pending. Retire held the session mutation gate while it waited for
  room on the loop's bounded wake channel, and the loop takes that gate to
  process each wake, so a burst of admissions behind a held loop (a mob stop
  holds run starts) could leave both waiting forever. A full wake channel
  already guarantees the loop wakes, so retire now counts it as woken; only a
  closed channel means there is no loop.

- `meerkat-runtime`: a reset, destroy or retire whose caller is dropped
  mid-operation (a JSON-RPC request aborted after EOF or SIGTERM, an aborted
  mob task, a cancelled schedule host) completes. The operation ran in its
  caller's task, so the drop could leave the registration reload-required,
  or a retired session with pending inputs that never ended; once it holds
  the session's mutation gate, it now runs in its own task.

- `meerkat-runtime`: an embedder that gives a session an executor without
  binding it to a runtime placement (`prepare_bindings`) now gets a typed
  refusal (`RuntimeDriverError::ValidationFailed`) when it admits a directed
  input, before anything is queued. Such an input could never be published,
  since a directed terminal names the runtime placement, and the session's
  next stop or retire failed after its checkpoint and left the registration
  reload-required.

- `meerkat-runtime`: when a retire or an archive fails at a step after its
  durable commit (the session's machine commit, the archive's model-routing
  handoffs, its post-commit hook, or the removal of a recovered
  registration), the waiters of the inputs it ended are still answered and
  their completions recorded before the error is returned. They used to wait
  for a recovery that a retired session never runs.

- `meerkat-runtime`: a Reset the machine refuses, on a running or a stopped
  runtime, answers `RuntimeControlPlaneError::InvalidState { state }`
  (`RuntimeDriverError::NotReady { state }` through
  `SessionServiceRuntimeExt::reset_runtime`) before it ends a resumable run or
  prepares anything. It used to prepare its inputs' terminals first and roll
  them back once the machine refused, which marked the registration
  reload-required and answered an internal error.

- `meerkat-rpc`, `rkat`: a mob member whose runtime is repair-blocked retires
  on the JSON-RPC host and under `rkat mob`. A member is repair-blocked when
  the store refused one of its runtime's commits, so its runtime waits for a
  reload. Retiring such a member reloads its runtime from durable state, moves
  the member's operation onto the reloaded runtime, and archives through a
  hook that marks that operation retired once the runtime is durably Retired.
  Neither host's mob session service passed the hook on to the persistent
  session service it wraps. The trait default refused it, so the retirement
  failed with `MobError::MemberRetirementStuck` at `retire-session-archive`
  ("session service cannot run a pre-retire archive hook"). Every redrive
  failed the same way, and the member stayed Retiring. This has been so since
  0.8.22 and shipped in 0.9.4: `RpcMobSessionService` in `meerkat-rpc` and
  `MobCliSessionService` in `rkat` forwarded only the archives without a
  hook. Both now forward the hook-bearing archive.

- `meerkat-rpc`, `rkat`: a member identity that converged keeps reconciling
  on the JSON-RPC host and under `rkat mob`. After a member identity
  converges, each later reconciliation pass checks its cached session
  against the store's persisted session authority. Neither host's mob
  session service passed that read on to the persistent session service it
  wraps, and the trait default answers that the read is unsupported. Every
  later reconciliation pass after convergence therefore failed ("session
  service cannot cheaply revalidate exact persisted authority") and went
  into backoff, so identity reconciliation stopped acting on that member. The
  JSON-RPC identity verbs (`mob/adopt_member_identity_declaration`) reach it.
  As shipped in 0.9.4, `meerkat-mob`'s `actor.rs:25253-25275` refuses the
  unsupported read, and `RpcMobSessionService` (`session_runtime.rs:1308`)
  and `MobCliSessionService` (`main.rs:16724`) keep the trait default
  (`session_service.rs:1471`). Both now forward the read cost and the read.

- `meerkat-rpc`: Rust embedders composing the RPC runtime's mob state
  (`meerkat_rpc::router::compose_rpc_mob_state`) get the persistent session
  service's answers on its mobs where 0.9.4 refused or reported nothing:
  - `MobHandle::activate_member_instruction` failed with "instruction
    activation is not supported by this session service";
  - with `openai-live`, `MemberHandle::start_live_bridge_operation` was
    rejected, because the member eligibility preflight refused;
  - a held spawn's `controller_route_report` was
    `ControllerRouteObservation::Unsupported`.

  As shipped in 0.9.4, `RpcMobSessionService` (`session_runtime.rs:1308`)
  kept those trait defaults (`meerkat-mob`'s `session_service.rs:1240`,
  `1307`, `1337` and `2202`). It now forwards them.

- RPC callback tools accept typed content blocks from SDK handlers, which
  released 0.9.3 and 0.9.4 rejected as non-string results. Mixed text and image
  results are preserved alongside legacy text and tool error flags.
- `meerkat-session`, `meerkat-mob`: a member retired while its turn sat
  between the turn's end-of-run checkpoint and its runtime boundary commit
  (the retirement's boundary cancel lands between the two) retires instead of
  stalling, and a mob destroy with such a member completes. That turn leaves
  a durable tail ahead of the runtime boundary, and every committed read of
  the session refused it with a transcript revision conflict. Once the live
  actor was gone, the reads that ask whether the member's session is still
  present before its archive (a retirement's route observation and archive
  stage check, a destroy's retire route and its archive disposal step) ended
  the operation on that refusal before the archive ran, the archive itself
  failed on it too, and the mob never observed the member archived. Those
  reads now take the refusal as proof that the session is still there and go
  on to the archive. The archive settles that tail itself, under the turn
  boundary and recovery gate it already holds, with the same store-owned
  recovery a restart runs, and reads the session again, whether or not the
  live actor is still hosted. A tail the recovery holds or refuses keeps its
  bytes and ends the archive, and the retirement or destroy, with the typed
  `SessionError::DurableTailHeldForRecovery` or
  `SessionError::DurableTailRecoveryRefused`.

- `meerkat`, `meerkat-runtime`, `meerkat-mob`, `meerkat-rpc`,
  `meerkat-mcp-server`: a restart refused before the session serves keeps the
  inputs it recovered. A materialization refused after its runtime
  registration recovered the session's inputs from the store (a durable tail
  held for recovery, a refused recovery, a failed agent build, a mob host's
  refusal) rolled the registration back with an unregister that stopped
  every non-terminal input. A held tail's stranded input was ended as
  stopped, the hold went with it, and the next start ran without the input.
  Every materialization rollback now unregisters with the generated Keep
  disposition: `PreparedSessionMaterialization::rollback_now` and
  `rollback_now_under_turn_finalization_boundary`, a prepared materialization
  dropped before it committed, and a refused or cancelled preparation. So
  does the retirement of an executor attachment that never served (a pending
  attachment's abort, the cleanup of a failed startup). A mob host's refusal
  of a restored member's registration asks for the same keep through the new
  public `UnregisterQueuedInputs::Keep`. Every input the registration
  recovered stays exactly as the store holds it, so the hold stands and a
  later start or the operator's repair runs the input once. The machine grants
  the keep only to a registration that served no live work: after an
  admission, a resubmission deduplicated onto an input it holds, or a host's
  recycle (whose recovery mixes live inputs into the recovered ones), the
  unregister records Stop and stops every input, so a turn whose caller saw
  the materialization refused never runs on a later start. A retire or an
  archive that meets an unserved attachment still stops every input. The keep
  is recorded with the unregister's progress (machine lifecycle record
  version 6), so a crash during the rollback replays it, and the next start
  keeps every input the store still holds open.

- `meerkat`, `meerkat-runtime`: a restart refused before the session serves
  keeps the inputs it recovered. A materialization refused after its runtime
  registration recovered the session's inputs from the store (a durable tail
  held for recovery, a refused recovery, a failed agent build) rolled the
  registration back with an unregister that stopped every non-terminal
  input. A held tail's stranded input was ended as stopped, the hold went
  with it, and the next start ran without the input. The rollback now
  unregisters with the generated Keep disposition: every input the
  registration recovered stays exactly as the store holds it, so the hold
  stands and a later start or the operator's repair runs the input once. An
  input admitted while the registration stood still ends as stopped. A
  refused preparation, and a cancelled one, keep the same way.
  `PreparedSessionMaterialization::rollback_now_keeping_recovered_inputs` is
  the rollback for a materialization that admitted no input; `rollback_now`
  still stops every input. The keep is recorded with the unregister's
  progress (machine lifecycle record version 6), so a crash during the
  rollback keeps the same inputs. The machine grants the keep only to a
  registration that served no live work: after an admission, a resubmission
  deduplicated onto an input it holds, or a host's recycle (whose recovery
  mixes live inputs into the recovered ones), the unregister records Stop
  and stops every input, so a turn whose caller saw the materialization
  refused never runs on a later start.

- `meerkat-gemini`: preserve provider-issued `functionCall.id` through
  streamed tool calls, saved transcripts, assistant replay and matching
  `functionResponse.id`, including parallel calls to the same function.
  Meerkat's internal tool correlation IDs remain separate and are never
  emitted as provider IDs when Gemini omitted the optional field.

- Continuations on a retired address. A continuation whose drain reserved it
  before a crash, on an address that retired since, no longer reads
  `pending` forever: the delivery owner settles the reservation from the
  reserved session's input ledger, under that session's custody, so it reads
  admitted when the input is there and stranded when it is not (another
  input under the key keeps the reservation, reported in the owner's pass).
  A `stranded` status is now final: a drain that resolved the address before
  it retired observes the address again after its reservation and before
  the admission, releases the reservation and admits nothing, and a status
  read reads the admission index again after it observed the retirement, so
  a resend under a new key is the only delivery. A host's
  `RuntimeDeliveryHost::observe_address` must agree on Retired with the
  continuation status read; both shipped hosts delegate to the bound
  resolver. A governed host original follows the same rules: its drain
  observes the address after the binder bound it and before native
  admission, and on a retired address releases the reservation and
  withdraws the binder's custody; the owner settles its reservation on a
  retired address by the reserved input id, since a governed admission is
  indexed under its qualified key.

- `meerkat`: a host that composes consent notices no longer refuses a
  retained completion of another producer drained before it binds its
  continuation services (for example by the arming reconcile after a
  restart). Its consent-aware job source answered such jobs absent, which
  refused the completion terminally; it now answers unavailable, so the
  completion stays pending until the bound owner decides it.

- `meerkat-core`, `meerkat-session`, `meerkat-runtime`, `meerkat-store`: a
  long run of a HeadCanonical session kept every compaction's transcript
  rewrite in memory until the run ended, because retirement may not pass the
  durable head and the run saved only at its end; the committed session then
  kept every rewrite of the run too. The run now moves its durable head at
  each of its round commits (see Changed), so it keeps at most one rewrite
  beyond `history_retained_rewrites` in memory, and the committed session
  keeps no more than the retention. Round commits prune no stored rewrite
  rows: the committed
  boundary stays rebuildable for recovery until the boundary commit that
  promotes the run, which applies the run's retention cut in its own
  transaction and never past the promoted head's row-lineage anchor. Before, a
  run that retired rewrites between two of its checkpoints could prune rows
  its committed boundary still needed, and a crash before the boundary commit
  then left a session that recovery could not rebuild.

- `meerkat-runtime`, `meerkat-store`, `meerkat-core`: a crash tail of a
  HeadCanonical session that had compacted at least once could not be
  recovered. A host that stopped after a run's final save and before that
  run's boundary commit (a crash, a forced kill, an out-of-memory kill) left
  the session unresumable: every later resume failed with an internal
  durable-tail recovery error, whether that run compacted or only appended
  rows. Recovery refused a session that carried its rewrite history, and it
  could not prove that a run whose compaction rewrote rows still descends from
  the committed boundary. It now accepts the history exactly as the store's
  physical head records it, and proves a rewritten tail's descent through the
  store's rewrite rows. Such a tail recovers like any other: a completed run
  becomes the recovered boundary, an interrupted run is closed with the typed
  recovery notice and is not requeued, and a tail recovery cannot classify, or
  whose descent the store cannot prove, is held with
  `SESSION_DURABLE_TAIL_HELD_FOR_RECOVERY` instead of an internal error.
  Sessions that 0.9.0 to 0.9.4 left in this state resume after upgrading, with
  no repair step, when their head records a graph prefix. Every host that
  keeps sessions in a persistent HeadCanonical store reaches this path,
  persistent Meta deployments included.

- A graceful mob Shutdown releases a member's identity reconcile lease once
  it has unregistered the member's runtime and the member's session actor has
  exited, so the next incarnation takes that identity at once. Before, every
  lease stayed until it expired (up to 30 seconds), and the next start waited
  on each one. A member whose unregister is still running, or whose session
  actor still lives, at the Shutdown's deadline keeps its lease, as do a
  retiring member and every member of a process that ends without a
  Shutdown.

- `meerkat-session`, `meerkat-core`, `meerkat-contracts`: a deferred
  `session/create` prompt that `live/open` staged
  (`DeferredPromptPolicy::Stage`) no longer disappears on the session's first
  runtime-authored turn, such as the next `turn/start`. That turn commits only
  its typed appends, so the prompt reached the run-start hooks and
  `RunStarted` but neither the transcript nor the model request. The prompt
  now joins the turn's committed rows: folded into its first user row (staged
  content first), or as a user row ahead of the turn's other appends when it
  has none, and the run-start hooks and `RunStarted` see exactly those rows. A
  turn that commits no user row (a pending continuation, a run-start veto, a
  refusal before the run) leaves the prompt pending, so it lands exactly once,
  also for a session persisted with a staged prompt by an earlier release. A
  turn whose input carries directed interaction custody is refused with the new
  `AgentError::StagedPromptDirectedTurnRefused` while a prompt is staged. A
  live open that finds the prompt still staged (a voice-first session)
  delivers it instead: the run-start hooks a turn carrying it would run admit
  it, and it is committed as the session's newest user row before the
  realtime seed is read, so the realtime model receives it once. A later
  first text turn does not deliver it again, and a prompt a text turn already
  delivered is never delivered by a later open. A hook that refuses it at the
  open keeps it staged for the first text turn; the open goes ahead without it
  and reports `staged_prompt_refused` in the result's new `advisories`. An
  open that never waits behind a running turn (the mirrored channel and the
  concurrent summary open) delivers it only when no turn holds the session's
  turn boundary.
- `meerkat-mob`: a member retirement whose member session degraded after
  its quiesce stage, for example a retire that waited there on a boundary
  commit that then passed its deadline, no longer sticks at its ingress
  detach. The runtime refused the detach of the degraded session
  (`RuntimeDriverError::RecoveryRepairBlocked`), the retirement stuck with
  an internal error, and a manual reload of the retiring member was refused
  too. The ingress detach now reloads the member session first, through the
  same durability reload as the quiesce stage and a destroy, and detaches
  the cold successor that reload published, so the retirement completes (on
  a plain retry when the caller's wait ended first). When the runtime
  refuses that reload as repair-blocked, or the session degrades after the
  stage's reload check, the retirement sticks with the typed
  `MobError::MemberReloadRepairBlocked`, and a redrive completes it once the
  runtime's evidence settles.
- A turn that compacts its history more often than
  `[compaction] history_retained_rewrites` keeps (five or more compactions at
  the default of 4) no longer ends at its intra-turn checkpoint on a
  HeadCanonical store with "failed to prove pending rewrite suffix:
  transcript revision ... was retired with N older rewrite(s)", which
  abandoned the turn. The agent checkpoints at the end of a run, so every
  compaction of the run lands before that checkpoint, and the checkpoint
  persists them by proving the rewrite graph's suffix from the head the run
  started on; compaction had already retired the bodies of the oldest of
  them. A session that a HeadCanonical head describes now keeps every rewrite
  occurrence that head does not cover yet, even past the retention bound, and
  retires down to the bound at its first compaction after a checkpoint covers
  them.
- `meerkat-schedule`, `meerkat`, `meerkat-store`, `meerkat-mob-mcp`: a
  scheduled delivery whose executor died after the target admitted it ended
  `misfired` under `skip` once its lease lapsed: the reclaim past the misfire
  deadline was refused, although the input had been admitted and could still
  complete. This lifts the 0.9.4 known limitation that such a delivery was
  reclaimed only inside its misfire window: keeping its crash recovery no
  longer needs a `catch_up_within` window longer than the lease. A reclaim
  now follows the misfire policy only when no earlier attempt recorded its
  dispatch:
  - an earlier attempt's admission is recorded (a `dispatch_accepted`
    receipt): the occurrence is reclaimed, also past its misfire deadline, for
    up to five attempts. The redelivery uses the runtime's deduplicate-only
    admission, so it finds the admitted input and never admits it again, and
    the occurrence records that input's outcome. For a mob member's session
    that admission is fenced like the first delivery's, to the member's
    executor attachment and residency; a refused fence admits nothing and
    leaves the occurrence to its next reclaim. A target still busy with
    that input does not end the redelivery under `skip_if_running`, since a
    redelivery starts no new run. After five lost executors it ends
    `delivery_failed` with `lease_lost`; an input the runtime no longer knows
    (a row that recovery discarded, a store-less runtime's archived input)
    ends it `delivery_failed` (failure class `runtime_rejected`) with nothing
    admitted. A host runnable keeps no admission record and runs again, so
    for host runnables the guarantee is at-least-once and relies on the
    runnable deduplicating on `delivery_idempotency_key`. A target delivery
    that keeps the default `deliver_existing_occurrence` redelivers through
    its ordinary delivery and relies on that delivery's durable
    deduplication;
  - only an earlier dispatch start is recorded: a reclaim past the deadline
    asks the target, a busy one too, whether it admitted the delivery. It
    records that input's outcome when the target did, and ends `misfired`
    with nothing delivered when it did not. A mob target answers from its
    durable external-delivery record and begins none, and so does a mob
    member's identity target, on every surface (JSON-RPC and CLI included);
  - no dispatch was recorded (a crash before the dispatch start was
    recorded): the misfire policy decides, as before.
  The evidence is read from the occurrence's receipt history in both stores,
  so no column and no schema step is added. SQLite reads only the stage of
  each receipt of a reclaimed row, so a receipt whose other fields do not
  decode (a value a newer release wrote, read after a downgrade) does not pin
  the row; a receipt whose stage does not decode is the row's fault.
  The scheduling guide also names the failure class that the 0.9.4
  `runtime_completion_authority_unavailable` end is recorded with:
  `internal_error`.
