- `meerkat-schedule`: a scheduled delivery's lease is renewed while the
  target admits the delivery, not only while the delivery runs. An admission
  slower than the lease (60 seconds by default), such as a cold executor
  rebuild or a mob delivery's begin, let the lease lapse during the call; a
  reclaim could then take the occurrence while the input ran, spending one of
  its five attempts, and end it `delivery_failed` with `lease_lost`.

- `SqliteSessionStore::list` and `load_meta` no longer fail now and then
  with `SessionStoreError::Corrupted` for an intact HeadCanonical session
  while a commit to that session lands. Each read took the session's head
  row and the metadata cells that head names in separate snapshots, so a
  commit between the two paired the old head with the new metadata. Both
  reads now take the head and its metadata from one read transaction.

- `meerkat-mob`: a mob start no longer settles a durable tail on a retiring
  member's session that another runtime owner on the realm hosts. The restore
  of a retiring member's cleanup delivery settled such a tail (a turn's rows
  that landed after its runtime boundary) without the session's hosting claim,
  so it could adopt another process's in-flight tail. It now settles the tail
  under this runtime owner's claim through the new
  `MobSessionService::settle_durable_tail_before_cold_start`, which the
  persistent session service implements with its cold-attach preparation. The
  method's default settles through the resume verdict, which takes the claim
  as well (see the next entry) but materializes the whole resume, so a
  session-service wrapper around a persistent service should forward it, and
  `MobSessionService::settle_durable_tail_before_cold_start_reporting` too
  (see Added, a mob start after a graceful stop with a member's run in
  flight). When
  that claim is refused (`SessionError::ServedElsewhere` or
  `HostingUnavailable`), or the tail's recovery cannot prove it
  (`MobError::MemberDurableTailUnprovable`), the start defers that one member:
  the mob runs, the member stays Retiring with its tail untouched, and every
  operation on it (retire, `MobHandle::redrive_retirement`, respawn, destroy,
  the identity reconcile's retirement) re-attempts the restore first and,
  while it still fails, answers `MobError::MemberCustodyDeferred` without
  acting; a destroy refuses before it retires anything. The mob also
  re-attempts the restore on its own, on the identity reconcile's backoff (250
  ms doubling to 60 s), and once it succeeds the member's started retirement
  is re-driven and completes. Any other restore failure still fails the start.

- `meerkat-session`, `meerkat-mob`: resuming a session no longer settles a
  durable tail on a session that another runtime owner on the realm hosts.
  `PersistentSessionService::prepare_committed_boundary_resume` and
  `recover_committed_boundary`, which every persistent resume runs (a mob
  start's member restore, a resume spawn or respawn, a host
  materialization, an attached actor's recovery), recovered the tail
  without the session's hosting claim: a mob start adopted another
  process's in-flight tail on an active member's session, then stopped the
  mob when it bound the member. Both now take this runtime owner's claim
  first and refuse with `SessionError::ServedElsewhere`, or
  `HostingUnavailable` when the claim cannot be taken, before any recovery;
  the tail stays as it was. `MobBuilder::resume` returns that error, and the
  error log names the member, its session and the remedy (stop that runtime
  owner, or wait until it releases the session, then start again). A
  resume spawn of such a session returns it too, where it failed with an
  internal error before.

- `meerkat-mob`: a mob start no longer stops over a member whose restore
  failed at that start (its spawn customizer refused it, say). The start read
  that member's session to restore its operation binding, met a durable tail
  as a transcript revision conflict, and stopped the whole mob, at every
  start. It now settles the tail under this runtime owner's hosting claim, as
  it does for a retiring member's, and reads the session again. When it still
  cannot restore the binding because another runtime owner hosts the member's
  session, its hosting claim cannot be taken, or its durable tail could not be
  proven, the mob runs, the member stays Broken, and its custody restore is
  deferred, which the member's status shows (`custody_deferred`). A respawn, a
  retire, a destroy, an explicit resume and the identity reconcile each
  re-attempt the restore first. While it still cannot restore, a respawn, a
  retire and a destroy refuse with `MobError::MemberCustodyDeferred` and leave
  the member's session as it was, an explicit resume still succeeds, and the
  reconcile backs off. Once the cause clears, the next of them, or the mob's
  own backoff, restores the member's custody and proceeds. Any other restore
  failure, such as a restore tuple that diverges from the mob's authority or a
  session store failure, still stops the start.

- `meerkat-mob`: a mob start that cannot restore a member because another
  runtime owner hosts its session reports the typed hosting refusal as the
  startup failure's cause wherever the start prepares the member's runtime
  bindings, not an internal preparation error. A member whose durable tail its
  store-owned recovery kept (it could not prove the tail) is reported as
  `MobError::MemberDurableTailUnprovable`, naming the member and its session
  and carrying the `tail_held_for_recovery` resume hold, instead of a bare
  transcript revision conflict. Where the start still fails on such a member,
  that typed cause is what it reports; a retiring member, or one whose restore
  already failed, is deferred instead (see the entries above).

- `meerkat-mob`: a mob start no longer stops over a member whose session
  runtime was retired or destroyed outside the mob, by a host's direct
  `retire_runtime_control_plane` or `RuntimeControlPlane::destroy` rather
  than the mob's own retire flow. The start's readiness pass still targeted
  the member, found its comms runtime gone with it, and stopped the whole mob
  (`MobError::MissingMemberCapability`). The pass now leaves that member out
  and records it Broken with a typed restore failure that says how its
  runtime ended outside the mob and to respawn the member; the mob serves its
  other members. Only the runtime's own `Retired` or `Destroyed` state leaves
  a member out.

- `meerkat-mob`, `meerkat-machine-schema`, `meerkat-machine-kernels`:
  destroying one member's session runtime outside the mob
  (`RuntimeControlPlane::destroy` on the member's runtime id) no longer
  destroys the whole mob. The runtime's `RuntimeDestroyed` reaches the mob as
  `ObserveRuntimeDestroyed`, and MobMachine cleared every member and moved
  the mob to Destroyed for any live, fence-matched member runtime. The
  observation now removes only that runtime, in a Running, Stopped or
  Completed mob (`ObserveRuntimeDestroyed` and the new
  `ObserveRuntimeDestroyedStopped` and `ObserveRuntimeDestroyedCompleted`),
  as a runtime retired outside the mob is removed: the mob keeps its phase,
  its other members and its active runs, and the member is Broken at its
  next start (see the entry above). It also advances the topology epoch, so
  a trust permission minted against the member's earlier eligibility is
  stale. The same holds during the mob's own destroy: a member runtime
  destroyed after an attempt returned `MobDestroyError::Incomplete` (an
  operator unsticking the destroy, say) ended the mob without the destroy's
  drains, and the retry then skipped the member retirements, the host
  revokes and the Destroy input, so a bound host was never revoked. The mob
  is now Destroyed only through its Destroy input, after `RevokeHost` and
  every drain (see Breaking for the new `TransitionId` values). The member
  lifecycle TLC audit (`specs/machines/mob_machine/member_lifecycle_audit.sh`)
  now checks the destroy admission, and that a destroyed runtime removes
  only itself (`AuditRuntimeDestroyedRemovesOnlyItsRuntime`).

- `meerkat-mob`, `meerkat-machine-schema`: a mob whose member's session
  runtime ended outside it (retired or destroyed through the runtime control
  plane) can be destroyed. The destroy's retirement admission had no arm for
  a member whose runtime is gone while its identity is still bound, so every
  destroy attempt returned `MobDestroyError::Incomplete`. The new
  `AdmitDestroyMemberRetireRuntimeEnded` arms (Running, Stopped) mark the
  member Retiring with its retirement session and request its session
  ingress detach, with no runtime retire, and the destroy archives it as a
  retired member. A mob with a member retired outside it could not be
  destroyed in 0.9.4 either.

- `meerkat-mob`, `meerkat-machine-schema`: the mob's active run count is
  now right. As in 0.9.4, a member runtime retired outside the mob
  (`ObserveRuntimeRetired`, in Running and Stopped) and every member
  retirement archive (the ordinary, destroy, placed and remote archive arms
  taken while the runtime was still live) set the mob-wide count to zero
  while another member's flow run was still active: `MobHandle::stop` was
  then admitted under that run, and cancelled it at a boundary; it is now
  refused with `MobError::InvalidTransition` until the run ends. Only the
  arms that end every run of the mob (stop, complete, reset, force cancel,
  shutdown, destroy, cancel all work) reset the count now. An external
  delivery whose Flow admission fails after the run started (its
  realization claim fails, or the delivery turns terminal before the Flow
  realizes it) now ends that run (`FinishRun`) as well as its Flow: the
  compensation left the count at one, which those resets hid, so the stop
  was refused until a cancel-all, force cancel, shutdown or destroy.

- `meerkat-mob`: a resume spawn onto a session whose durable tail runs past
  its committed runtime boundary, and which no start of the mob restores
  (another mob's member session, say), now refuses with that typed
  transcript revision conflict (`SessionError::Store`) instead of an
  internal "resume bridge session check failed" error. The spawn does not
  settle the tail; it stays as it was. On a WholeBlob store, whose committed
  read never refuses under a tail, a session no live actor hosts is refused
  with `SessionError::DurableTailHeldForRecovery` instead, decided by the new
  `MobSessionService::provisional_tail_stands`. A session-service wrapper
  around a persistent service must forward it: its default refuses with
  `SessionError::Unsupported` for a service that reports persistent
  sessions, so the spawn refuses rather than skipping the check.
- `meerkat-mob`, `meerkat-schedule`, `meerkat-mob-mcp`: a bounded helper or
  bounded fork child with runtime mode `autonomous_host` is now refused with
  `UnsupportedForMode` before anything is spawned. This covers `spawn_helper`
  and `fork_helper`, `fork_member_then_run_bounded` and
  `fork_member_then_run_detached`, RPC `mob/spawn_helper` and
  `mob/fork_helper`, and scheduled helper targets.
  Before, the helper was spawned and its autonomous kickoff turn ran (one
  model request) before the bounded task failed, because autonomous inbox
  delivery has no tracked turn completion. Schedules now refuse such a helper
  target at create and update, and a schedule stored with one fails each
  occurrence before any spawn. A bounded fork child whose spec names no
  runtime mode now runs turn-driven, as a bounded helper does, instead of
  inheriting an autonomous profile default and failing the same way.

- `meerkat-mob`: an identity whose lease claim meets a live holder retries
  as soon as that holder's lease expires. Reconciliation claims a lease it
  reads as expired, and the claim can still find it held: another
  incarnation claimed it in between, or the identity store's clock runs
  behind the actor's. Such an identity stayed unreconciled until the slow
  safety scan, about five minutes later; it now waits for the holder's
  expiry, at least one second, the same way as `AwaitLease`.

- `meerkat-mob`: a Destroy of a Stopped mob no longer fails with
  `MobDestroyError::Incomplete` at every attempt when the mob's routed queue
  still holds a member route that the member's runtime refused. While the
  mob is Stopped the mob machine cannot take that refusal, so the route
  waited for a resume, and each destroy attempt dispatched it again and
  stopped on the refusal until a resume or a restart emptied the queue. A
  destroy now drops its members' queued runtime-binding and input routes
  before it dispatches anything; it still sends their retire routes.

- The first restore after a process exit that cut a member's runtime
  unregister no longer leaves the member Broken. That restore concludes the
  cut teardown and then registers the session again, but the teardown fenced
  the restoring caller's materialization claim: the fresh registration was
  refused as owned elsewhere, and only a second restore brought the member
  back. The recovered drain now carries a claim of its own, so the caller's
  claim reaches the fresh registration untouched.

- `meerkat-auth-core`, `meerkat-runtime`, `meerkat-mob`: the published
  packages' own tests now build and pass standalone, with no library change.
  In 0.9.4, plain `cargo test` in the unpacked package did not compile
  auth-core's lib tests (a test helper used `meerkat-runtime`, a
  dev-dependency the package does not carry), nor runtime's and mob's
  default-feature test targets (one test file needed `sqlite-store` and
  `test-support`, one test needed `test-support`). With the command its
  README prints, one runtime lib test failed, because it read a meerkat-core
  fixture the runtime package did not ship; the package now ships it. The
  static standalone guard now also follows a `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` join
  through a same-file string constant.

- `meerkat-mob`: a mob whose startup recovery fails now tells its caller why.
  When the actor's durable recovery failed before it admitted a command,
  `MobHandle::status` reported only "mob actor reply channel closed" and
  `MobHandle::resume` only `ActorCommandChannelClosed`: the member, its
  session and the cause reached only the host's error log. Both now return the
  failure, typed, as `MobError::SharedLifecycleFailure`. A member's failure is
  the new `MobError::MemberStartupRecoveryFailed`, which names the member, its
  session and the typed cause (such as `SessionError::ServedElsewhere`); its
  wire code and failure class are the cause's. Other commands on that handle
  still fail with `ActorCommandChannelClosed`, and `MobBuilder::resume` still
  returns the handle before startup recovery runs: read `MobHandle::status`
  for the reason. An actor that stops later because a durable mutation's
  outcome stayed uncertain reports that the same way, as the new
  `MobError::DurabilityFailStop`, whose cause is that mutation's own error.

- A durable session resumed with `provider` in a mob profile's
  `resume_overrides` (or a surface resume that changes provider) after the
  profile moved to another provider no longer fails with
  `ProviderMismatch` ("binding 'global:openai' resolves backend=OpenAI
  auth=OpenAI, expected provider Anthropic"), leaving a Meta identity Broken.
  Both resume merges restored the old provider's binding under the new
  provider. One Core rule now decides the resumed identity for the mob merge,
  the factory merge, the surface recovery merge and the member-host preflight:
  the durable binding is kept while the provider is unchanged, and a changed
  provider resolves its binding from the session's realm as a fresh member
  would (the realm's binding, then the parent realms and `global`, then the
  environment key). A binding backed by a credential account keeps its
  account, by the hot swap's affinity rule, or the resume refuses with the
  typed `NoCredentialAccountRoute` and leaves the durable session untouched.
  The history replays to the new provider without the old provider's native
  reasoning items. A name re-pointed in configuration at the new provider is
  not reused: the new provider's route is resolved afresh. Hosts that run
  members for other hosts need this release to resume such members.

- A connector OAuth login on one of its client profile's
  `registered_redirect_uris` can complete over RPC: `auth/login/start`
  returns its `host_attempt_handle`, and `auth/login/complete` passes the
  one the host sends (before, RPC dropped it both ways, so such a login was
  always refused as needing the host's custody). Without the handle the
  refusal carries `error.data.detail` `remote_custody_required` and leaves
  the attempt pending. `iss` stays MCP-only.

- `meerkat-runtime`: a browser OAuth completion on another redirect than the
  one its attempt was started on is refused as the caller's mismatched
  attempt (`OAuthFlowError::RedirectUriMismatch`: wire reason
  `attempt_mismatch`, RPC `INVALID_PARAMS`, REST 400), not as a flow-owner
  lifecycle failure (wire reason `infrastructure`, RPC `INTERNAL_ERROR`, REST
  500) that a host would retry. The runtime's flow owner checks a completion
  against the attempt its AuthMachine admitted, which refused another
  redirect only as a rejected transition; the machine's own record of the
  attempt now tells that case apart. This covers a loopback MCP login and a
  provider browser login; a completion for another provider keeps its
  lifecycle rejection.

- `meerkat-mob-mcp`, `meerkat-rpc`, `meerkat-web-runtime`: a mob whose actor
  has stopped (it fail-stopped, or its task ended while the mob was live) is
  no longer listed as if it ran. `mob/list`, the MCP `meerkat_mob_list` and
  agent `mob_list` tools, the Web runtime's `listMobs` and the TypeScript
  SDK's `listMobs` give its row a typed `failure`: present means the mob's
  actor has stopped; `status` is the last machine phase. The Python SDK's
  `list_mobs` returns the row as it is. Before, the row read `Running` and
  nothing else, while `mob/status` reported the failure.
  `MobHandle::status_observation_snapshot` is still the phase alone; its
  documentation now says so and points to `lifecycle_observation`.

- `meerkat-mob`: a handle of a mob whose actor stopped no longer binds a
  continuation for a mob the host holds again under the same id.
  `MobHandle::submit_continuation` and `submit_retained_continuation` bind
  to the handle's own mob incarnation, so such a handle answers
  `OwnerRetired` and commits nothing for the new mob's member. Before, only
  a destroyed mob's handle was refused, because a stopped actor's handle
  keeps its last live phase.

- `meerkat-mob`: a mob host that fail-stops on a durable write whose outcome
  stayed uncertain names the first such write in every refusal after it.
  Before, a later uncertain write in the same process could replace it, so
  the refusals named a consequence instead of the cause. The detail is the
  host's typed error (`MobHostActorError`); where the host built the detail
  itself it now reads `durable host binding outcome is uncertain: ...`. The
  refusals keep their cause (`Internal`) and their "restart required" prefix.

- An authorization server that accepts a request and never answers no longer
  holds an MCP login, its host or the credential forever. A start that
  stalls ends typed (`upstream_failure`, detail `upstream_timeout`) and
  admits nothing, so the server's next start is not queued behind it. A
  completion that stalls ends typed (detail `upstream_timeout` before the
  authorization code was sent, `upstream_timeout_after_code` after), its
  attempt retired and nothing published. Cancelling the attempt by its
  reference while its `auth/login/complete` is in flight ends that call at
  once (`attempt_missing`); a cancel answered `cancelled: true` means nothing
  from that attempt is ever published. A refresh whose token endpoint never
  answers fails transiently at its bound and keeps the credential, where it
  held the credential's exclusive mutation without bound, so a login of the
  same server (or its logout) waited forever. A credential commit that does
  not report in time ends as `commit_unsettled`, never as a success or a
  clean failure; `rkat-rpc` notes it for shutdown, so its attempt is never
  reported as cleanly resolved.

- A quiet store no longer wakes its own readers. The SQLite change watch
  counted a connection's own open and close (the first connection creates
  the WAL and the WAL index, the last removes them) as a store change, so a
  read that opened the database woke the next one. On a quiet store the
  delivery owner's kept generation reader reopened itself 10 to 30 ms after
  each idle release, and so held its connection, with the presence lock the
  maintenance fence waits for, nearly all the time; the fresh-open read
  path, which Windows takes, could open the database tens of times a
  second; and a mob event observer's catch-up reads woke it about 90 times
  a second. Commits still wake them at once, and the watch's sweep still
  bounds a missed notification. On the fresh-open path, a notification
  after which the database and its WAL stat as they did before the last
  read (a platform that reports a read's own open or close as a change of
  the WAL) is answered from that read without opening the database; a
  sweep always reads.
- `@rkat/web`: a destroy that did not finish (`Mob.lifecycle("destroy")`,
  `Session.destroy()` of a session that owns mobs, or
  `MeerkatRuntime.destroy()`) no longer loses its report. The runtime's
  error envelope carried the report only at its top level, and
  `MeerkatError.fromWasm` keeps an envelope's `data`; `Mob.lifecycle()`
  rejected with the raw envelope string. The envelope now also carries the
  typed incomplete data under `data`, as JSON-RPC sends it in `error.data`,
  and `mobDestroyIncompleteReport(error)` reads the report.

- An MCP connect under the interactive auth mode no longer waits out the
  300 s interactive login window when it cannot open a login. Only a remote
  server with an auth resolver gets the window; a stdio server, and a remote
  server without a resolver, are bounded by their own
  `connect_timeout_secs`. A member router built by the factory uses the
  interactive mode, so a stdio server that never speaks MCP held a member's
  connect until its process exited, or for about 5 minutes when it hung; it
  now fails at its connect timeout. A failed connect closes a stdio server
  whose initialize handshake never completed, with an EOF grace of at most
  250 ms (the stdio close bounds' own, if shorter) and its TERM grace, so the
  connect ends within its connect timeout plus at most 0.25 s, or plus the
  TERM grace for a server that ignores SIGTERM. A server that did complete
  initialize keeps its full close grace. A connect that runs out of time
  names the deadline it had ("after 301s (1s connect timeout and the 300s
  interactive login window)"). No public API changes.

- Streamed model text keeps a character that a network chunk boundary split
  intact. The OpenAI Responses, OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions, OpenAI
  streamed image, Anthropic and Gemini stream readers decoded every network
  chunk on its own before splitting it into lines, so a multi-byte character
  (a typographic apostrophe, an emoji) that straddled two chunks became
  U+FFFD in the streamed text, the live events and the stored history. The
  readers now keep the bytes until a line is complete and decode each
  complete line strictly (`meerkat_llm_core::streaming::Utf8LineBuffer`). A
  complete line that is not valid UTF-8 fails the stream as a stream parse
  error instead of being replaced; after an OpenAI-compatible stream's finish
  it ends the stream, like any other undecodable line there. Bytes after the
  last line break are treated as before: the Anthropic reader still reads
  them as a last line, now decoded as strictly, and an OpenAI-compatible
  stream that ends inside a line before its finish is still an incomplete
  response, also when it ends inside a character.

- The TypeScript SDK decodes a child process's stderr as one stream, so a
  character that a pipe read split stays intact in the stderr that a
  `PROCESS_EXITED` or `ARCHIVE_EXTRACT_FAILED` error carries (it became
  U+FFFD), and the stderr tail of a `PROCESS_EXITED` error never starts with
  half of a surrogate pair.

- `meerkat-core`: a model call is no longer aborted as a stalled stream before
  it ran. The stream inactivity watchdog checked its window before it first
  polled the call, so on a starved runtime its first check could come a whole
  window after the call started and abort a call that had never run; the
  turn then spent a retry on it, or failed once its retries were spent. The
  call now runs once first, and its inactivity counts from then.

- `meerkat-core`: a tool call admitted after its deadline now times out
  instead of entering its body. A call waiting for a dispatch slot whose
  deadline passed in the same scheduler turn the slot came free (a starved
  runtime notices both at once) was admitted and ran.

- `meerkat-sqlite`: on macOS, dropping a SQLite store watch no longer blocks
  the dropping thread on file-system event service round trips. A stopped
  watch's FSEvents source is dropped on the process's one unregister thread;
  sources stopped together wait in its queue.

- `meerkat-mob`: a resume spawn of an existing session (a `Resume` launch,
  such as a host re-materializing a retired member, or a spawn with
  `resume_session_id`) no longer runs the member's first turn again. An
  autonomous member got a fresh kickoff turn (its initial message, or the
  fallback role prompt) and a turn-driven member re-ran its initial message
  on every resume, each appending a manufactured turn and a model request to
  the existing transcript. A resume now delivers the first turn only while
  the session's first turn never started (its deferred first-turn phase is
  still pending, or it is a deferred template), and then once; otherwise it
  runs no kickoff and does not deliver `initial_message`, and it logs the
  undelivered message at info. A first turn that started and was interrupted
  is not re-run. Fresh spawns, fork seatings and identity reconciliation are
  unchanged. Placed members (`placement` set) get the same rule (see the
  placed resume entry below). `meerkat-core` adds
  `Session::is_deferred_template`, the one predicate the session service and
  the mob read for a deferred template.

- `meerkat-session`: a session resumed while its first turn was still pending
  now records that first turn's start durably. A run checkpoint persisted the
  deferred-turn state the resumed agent was built from, so after the first
  turn ran the store still said it was pending: every later resume marked the
  first turn pending again and reopened its build-override window. A
  checkpoint now persists the session's live deferred-turn state, the value an
  export already wrote. A session that carries no deferred-turn state is
  persisted as before.

- `meerkat-mob`: a placed member's resume (`placement` set with a `Resume`
  launch) no longer runs the member's first turn again; it follows the rule
  of the resume entry above. Only the member host can read the adopted
  session, so the controller first asks the host with `HostFeatures`, before
  anything is recorded, and sends a host that lists `adopted_first_turn` the
  resume as protocol 7 with `report_adopted_first_turn`; the ack reports
  whether the session's first turn started. A started first turn waives the
  kickoff: an autonomous member's committed placed-spawn carrier records the
  waiver (`adopted_first_turn_started`), so cold recovery repairs no kickoff
  for it, and a turn-driven member's initial message is not delivered and
  not recorded. An ack that omits a report its request asked for, reports
  one it did not ask for, or names a launch outcome that contradicts its
  launch fails the spawn with `MobError::WiringError`, and the member is
  released. A probe that fails for another reason than an old host (no
  answer within 10 seconds, transport, admission) fails the resume with
  `MobError::HostFeaturesProbeFailed` before anything is recorded. Fork
  seatings, including the capability-attached seating, keep their kickoff.
  Mixed fleet: a member host of 0.9.4 or earlier refuses the probe and
  reports nothing, so a resume there still runs the first turn until that
  host is upgraded. Downgrade: only a waived carrier record carries the new
  key, and a 0.9.4 controller refuses it (`deny_unknown_fields`): it does
  not restore a mob that holds such a member, and `MobBuilder::resume`
  fails with `MobError::StorageError` (a serialization error that names
  `adopted_first_turn_started`). A 0.9.4 member host reads a materialized
  member row that carries the new `adopted_first_turn` key and ignores it.

- `meerkat-mob`: a turn-driven placed spawn (`placement` set) with an
  `initial_message` no longer always fails. The member was materialized and
  committed on its host, then the spawn refused to admit its first turn
  with an internal "resolved to a placed admission" error and unwound. The
  initial message is now delivered to the member through the placed
  delivery lane an ordinary member send uses. A delivery the member refuses
  fails the spawn with that typed refusal, and the member is released. No
  durable intent covers this first turn, so a controller crash before its
  delivery loses it.

- A durable fork child's model no longer reads the bodies of activation
  rows and skills it copied from its source when the fork instruction
  policy does not carry them, and a malformed activation row now refuses
  the model request instead of reaching the model as stored.

- A prompt-context fork no longer hands its source's activated instruction
  bodies or the skill bodies its source loaded with `load_skill` to the
  child as plain context under the default fork instruction policy, and
  the `refuse` policy now refuses such a fork. The renderer copied every
  System row of the source, its system prompt and activation envelopes
  included, and every tool result, under every policy. The rows are now
  decided by their typed activation identity and by the tool call that
  produced them, never by their text (see Breaking).
- A prompt-context fork child now reads the peer traffic in its source's
  history: whom the source heard from (or wrote to), the text of a peer
  message, a status and a payload preview (a request's params, a
  response's result) when the notice has them, and the sender's taint
  marker. The child was given only each notice's title ("Peer message",
  "Peer request: review"). The means to answer a peer (request and
  delivery ids, reply instructions) are not carried: the child is not
  the addressee.

- A turn-driven `MobHandle::fork_helper` (the default helper mode) now sees
  its fork context. The helper is created without an initial message, so
  the rendered context went into a deferred create request that discards
  its prompt, and the helper received only its task. The planned context
  is now recorded on the child's session and delivered before its first
  input, as a typed row (see Breaking). So does a helper placed on a
  member host that serves protocol 7 prompt-context forks; a turn-driven
  fork child placed on a host of 0.9.4 or earlier without an initial
  message still receives no fork context.

- `meerkat-core`, `meerkat-sqlite`, `meerkat-runtime`, `meerkat-session`,
  `meerkat-authorization`, `meerkat-auth-core`: a file lock released by its
  holder is now unlocked before its file closes: config document custody,
  session hosting claims and the cold-delivery owner lock, the SQLite
  maintenance fence with its operation and presence guards, runtime
  execution custody, the durable grant owner's lease, the credential
  refresh lock and the session event sequence lock. A process spawned
  meanwhile holds a copy of the holder's descriptor until it executes its
  program, and that copy kept a lock released by the close alone, so a
  single-try claim right after the release could be refused as held (for
  example, a governed MCP decision refused as not current).

- An MCP cancel by attempt reference
  (`McpOAuthAuthority::cancel_attempt_by_ref`,
  `HostAuthService::mcp_login_cancel_by_attempt_ref`) retires an attempt
  the flow owner holds without its payload, such as one a failed start
  could not retire, with any durable entry for it. It answered `Missing`
  while the attempt stayed admitted, holding the slot's flow capacity until
  a logout or a restart. `Missing` now means nothing with that reference is
  held.

- A failed MCP login start whose durable write failed after it committed no
  longer leaves the attempt's durable entry behind. The next read restored
  the entry as a pending attempt no browser could complete, which a status
  read reported until the attempt expired or a later start retired it.

- `meerkat-core`: a model response that stops at the token limit after reasoning, with no visible text or tool
  call, now ends the turn with the typed `MaxTokensReached` failure, even when the provider reports the
  reasoning only in its usage. Before, it was retried as empty output, or accepted as an empty completion after a
  tool call. Its usage is still charged.

- `meerkat-core`: a compaction summary call that came back with an empty summary, or whose rebuilt history was
  rejected, is now charged to the session's usage. Before, that provider call was dropped from accounting.

- Python SDK: `compaction_failed` events decode `reason` as the tagged object the runtime sends
  (`{"kind": ...}`), keeping every field and future reason kinds. Before, valid events were reported as
  malformed.

- Python SDK: a history row or assistant block whose provider metadata is
  `open_ai_assistant_message` is read instead of refused. Core has stored
  that metadata on every OpenAI Responses assistant message with an item id
  since 0.9.0, but the SDK's closed provider-metadata check did not list it,
  so reading such a session's history failed with `INVALID_RESPONSE`
  ("unsupported provider metadata"). The check now takes the variant's `id`,
  its optional `response_id` and its optional `phase` (`commentary` or
  `final_answer`), and keeps any other phase string as given. The TypeScript
  and Web SDKs never refused it.

- `meerkat-mob`, `meerkat-store`: a mob restarted after its process crashed,
  was killed or exited without a Shutdown kept every adopted identity's
  admission closed (`IdentityConvergenceAdmissionClosed`) until the earlier
  incarnation's identity reconcile lease expired, up to 30 s. A restart over a
  persistent store now takes such a lease at once when it can prove that the
  earlier process ended: a process holds an exclusive lock on
  `<mob store>.incarnation-custody` from before it mints its first
  incarnation until it exits, and marks the incarnations it mints under that
  lock. A restart in the same process, a restart while another process holds
  the lock, an incarnation minted without the lock (by an earlier version, or
  while another process held it) and a store without a file wait as before.
  `rkat storage doctor` lists the lock file as `mob-incarnation-custody-lock`,
  and `rkat storage prune` never removes it. `MobIdentityStore` gains the
  provided method `incarnation_custody_store` (default `None`).
- `meerkat`, `meerkat-rpc`: the session-scoped `live/open`, and the
  projection, refresh-config, identity and precheck reads behind it, restored
  a mob member's session from storage by its session id alone when it was
  not live, outside its mob (a member whose custody restore was deferred
  stays down), and the open went ahead on a member session that was live,
  with none of the checks the member's mob makes first (a member that is
  retiring, in cleanup or revoke, or whose restore failed). Both are now
  refused with `INVALID_PARAMS` (-32602) and data kind
  `mob_member_session_addressed_by_id` (with the session, mob and member):
  nothing is opened or restored, and `mob/member_live_open` opens the member
  through its mob, WebRTC included (see Breaking and Added).
  The reads behind a channel that already exists find a live member session
  as before.
  `SessionError::mob_member_session_addressed_by_id` and
  `SessionError::is_mob_member_session_addressed_by_id` name the refusal.
- `meerkat`: an agent built from an `AgentBuildConfig` whose mob tools are
  disabled (`override_mob` `Disable`) while it carries a generated mob
  operator authority context no longer mounts the factory's mob tool surface.
  Only an embedder that builds the config directly can set both (session
  build options resolve `Disable` to no authority context). The build's
  external mob operator tools were already bound to no authority, hidden and
  denying every call; the factory's own mob tools (`delegate`,
  `mob_spawn_member` and the rest) still mounted beside them.

- RPC session and mob streams retain their machine-authorized terminal
  notification when ordinary outbound byte or message admission is saturated.
  Reserved capacity follows the stream through close races, pending delivery and
  transport disconnect, without blocking the agent event producer.

- `meerkat-runtime`, `meerkat-session`: the archive of an ending session
  settles a durable tail when the session's runtime has stopped. When an
  input waited behind the boundary-cancelled turn, the runtime loop read the
  session's committed history before admitting it, met the tail, failed
  closed and left the runtime persisted `Stopped`. Durable-tail recovery
  counts a `Stopped` runtime as not quiescent, so the archive's recovery
  refused the tail and the retirement stayed stuck with
  `SessionError::DurableTailRecoveryRefused`. The new
  `recovery::recover_durable_tail_for_session_archive` is the store-owned
  recovery for an archive that holds the session's gates while the session
  ends, and the archive now uses it. Unlike ordinary recovery, it counts a
  persisted `Stopped` runtime as quiescent, as it counts a retired one, and
  it re-asserts `Stopped`. A persisted current run still refuses, and the
  commit stays fenced on the observed lifecycle row. Every other recovery
  still refuses a `Stopped` runtime, because a later start may resume its
  run.

- `meerkat-runtime`, `meerkat-session`: a live HeadCanonical session serves
  its next turn after a compaction that staged memory. After a compacting
  run's boundary, the runtime finalizes the compaction's projection intents
  in a metadata-only head commit that the live actor never prepared, so the
  actor's next checkpoint or boundary preparation (its next turn, or a live
  context append) was refused with "prepared metadata transition does not
  extend the observed head identity", until a resync on a later input. The
  live actor now adopts that commit as its metadata baseline after every
  finalization, after a run and in startup recovery.

- RPC session event subscriptions survive temporary outbound admission or
  notification-queue overflow. Before subsequent delivery they report lost
  events through the existing sequence-zero `StreamTruncated(StreamLagged)`
  marker. An unresolved gap at source end or close uses the reserved error
  terminal with its dropped count. This remains bounded, best-effort delivery;
  it does not replay lost events or change mob-stream overflow behavior.

- `meerkat-runtime`: a sweep of a runtime's pending inputs no longer abandons
  inputs that a store-owned durable-tail recovery already consumed. That
  recovery commits a tail at the store level and consumes the input rows
  bound to its run, outside the registered runtime's driver: an archive
  settles a tail it meets under its runtime lease, and an observation of a
  hosted session settles the tail a turn left when its boundary was
  cancelled (for example by a retirement). The driver still held those
  inputs as pending, so the next retire, reset, destroy, stop or
  queued-input cancel sweep wrote its abandonment (`Abandoned { Retired }`
  for a retire) over the consumed rows, and a directed input's sender was
  told that work which ran was terminated, so a peer could send it again.
  Every such sweep, and a replaced executor attachment's cleanup of its
  predecessor's inputs, now first adopts the `Consumed` terminals the store
  holds for inputs the driver still holds as pending, and leaves them
  consumed. A process-local waiter of such an input fails with
  `CompletionWaitError::AuthorityUnavailable` instead of being told the
  runtime terminated it; the input's result is in the session's committed
  history. An adoption that fails requires a registration-authorized cold
  reload of the runtime and fails the sweep.

- `meerkat-gemini`: a tool result's `functionResponse.response` uses
  Gemini's documented keys. A successful call's text is sent as
  `{"output": text}` and a failed call's as `{"error": text}`. Every result
  was sent as `{"content": text, "error": <is_error>}`, which names an
  `error` key even on success and no `output`, so the model could take a
  successful call as one that produced no output. The function response's
  `name` and `id`, the image parts that follow it and its lack of a thought
  signature are unchanged. The request bytes of every Gemini tool
  continuation change, so a resumed session takes one prompt-cache miss.

- `meerkat-gemini`: under authorization, a request that asks for Gemini's
  native search reaches the policy as the `GoogleSearch` hosted capability.
  The request names the tool `google_search`, which the capability check did
  not map, so the policy saw an unknown provider-native tool and a governed
  Gemini web search was refused as malformed.

- `meerkat-runtime`: a caller waiting on an input whose session's runtime
  must reload is answered once the runtime loop exits:
  `CompletionWaitError::AuthorityUnavailable`, which JSON-RPC `turn/start`
  answers with `-32603` and `data.reason` `completion_authority_unavailable`.
  When a run's boundary commit or terminalization got no durable outcome
  within the store's deadline, only that run's own inputs were answered
  (`DurableOutcomeUnknown`), and a caller waiting on an input queued behind
  the run got no answer until a reload or resume replaced the registration,
  and then only an untyped closed channel
  (`CompletionWaitError::ChannelClosed`). The input stays durably admitted
  and runs once the runtime reloads, so do not resubmit it: read it after
  the reload (see Session contracts).

- REST: a runtime apply whose session cannot be read fails, where it skipped
  the video input validation. `rkat`: a scheduled peer-ingress update fails
  on a session read error, where it turned keep-alive off.

- `meerkat-mob-mcp`: a fork-off re-link that cannot read the child's durable
  reply where it must decide (the job's limit, the commit ceiling, an idle
  child) delivers `restart_interrupted` carrying the read error and keeps the
  child seated. It took the failure for "no reply" and settled the job on
  that absence: past the job's limit it delivered `max_run_elapsed` and
  retired a child that may have replied, and at the commit ceiling it
  reported a commit that never landed.

- `meerkat-mob`: a member an adopted identity rebuilds (one that converged
  by retiring and respawning) keeps the tool bundles the mob registered for
  its profile, as a spawn of that profile does. The rebuild offered none of
  the bundles' tools.

- `meerkat-runtime`: `MeerkatMachine::with_admitted_original`,
  `MeerkatMachine::durable_admitted_original` and `verify_exact_replay` prove
  a keyed governed peer original, not only a prompt, so a source owner
  recovers custody of a governed peer after the payload is retired. A peer
  matches only under its exact input id and qualified key, with one own
  contributor of the same association and that contributor's canonical replay
  digest. An ungoverned peer, a key alone and a retained resume still refuse.
  Before, every peer was refused as a conflict
  (`crates/meerkat-runtime/src/meerkat_machine/admitted_original.rs:238` and
  `crates/meerkat-runtime/src/input_state.rs:1829` at v0.9.4).

### Security

- tokio is updated to 1.53.3 in Meerkat's lockfile for RUSTSEC-2026-0386.
  Meerkat's crates still accept tokio 1.43 and later, so a project that
  depends on them should update tokio to 1.53.3 or later in its own lockfile,
  for example with `cargo update -p tokio`.
- ctutils is updated to 0.4.5 in Meerkat's lockfile for RUSTSEC-2026-0385
  (reached only under the aws-sigv4 feature).
- RUSTSEC-2026-0387 (crypto-bigint) reaches only the optional live WebRTC
  path (meerkat-live's webrtc feature, used by openai-live), through webrtc
  0.14's dtls; it can expose timing of the per-handshake ECDHE secret.
  Builds without that feature are unaffected. The fix is porting meerkat-live
  to webrtc 0.20 or later, which is planned as a follow-up. The same optional
  path also carries the unmaintained audiopus_sys 0.2.2 (RUSTSEC-2026-0150,
  informational, no patched release).

### Upgrade notes

- Upgrade Core and its SDKs together: an SDK before 0.9.5 misreads a 0.9.5
  server's `tool_execution_completed`, and a 0.9.5 SDK sends its new request
  fields only to a 0.9.5 or later server (see Breaking).

- Upgrade the Meta gateway and Forge together. The Meta CHANGELOG carries the
  details.

- A `MobSessionService` wrapper outside this repository must forward
  `load_persisted_session_tolerating_tail` and `provisional_tail_stands` to
  its inner service. Without the first, mob reads of a member whose run
  holds a round commit keep the strict read and fail with a transcript
  revision conflict while the round's tail stands; without the second,
  every resume spawn over a persistent inner service is refused. It should
  forward `settle_durable_tail_before_cold_start`,
  `settle_durable_tail_before_cold_start_reporting`,
  `keeps_durable_member_sessions` and
  `materialize_session_resume_verdict_under_runtime_turn_boundary` as well:
  their defaults settle through a whole resume, report no continued run (so
  a mob start after a graceful stop with a member's run in flight fails),
  answer `supports_persistent_sessions` instead of the inner service's own
  answer, and make a member host's resume verdict wait for the turn
  boundary the host holds and refuse with `SessionError::Busy` once a
  durable tail stands.

- A `RuntimeStore` decorator outside this repository should forward
  `append_service_call_audit` and `read_service_call_audit`. Their defaults
  answer `Unsupported`, so every governed service call over the decorator is
  refused before it is sent.

### Known limitations

- A durable run that resumes asks the model again for a round that took no
  first commit: the round of a message that carries an image (the cursor
  rides the session head, which media externalization does not reach). A
  provider that mints fresh call ids for the repeated request (OpenAI,
  Anthropic) gives the repeated calls new dedupe keys; only a call with the
  same id, name and arguments meets the same key.
- A structured-output run that resumes after a crash during its extraction
  asks the model again from its last round commit, so it publishes
  `RunCompleted` with `extraction_required` a second time under the same run
  id.
- A WholeBlob run whose final save follows a compaction with no round commit
  since, and whose process stops before the run's boundary commit, is
  recovered as interrupted although its transcript is whole: that save
  re-based the run, so its rows are already the committed base, and the run
  shows the interrupted notice. Nothing is lost or run twice.
- A remote client (JSON-RPC or REST) whose turn on a durable session is in
  flight when the server stops gracefully, keeping the session's work, gets
  no typed suspended answer. Its request ends as a shutdown error: the
  session-not-running error with `kind: requeued_across_stop`, or a closed
  connection when the server exits first. The server resumes the run at its
  next start. Read the run's status before retrying: resubmitting the input
  runs it again.
- The usage of a model call that a restart interrupted is not recorded,
  although the provider bills it. Asynchronous operations a resumed run was
  waiting for ended with the restart: the run does not wait for them, and the
  model is told their results will not arrive. The tools of a resumed run see
  no current-turn content, as for a pending continuation, and the agent's
  lifetime budget counters restart with the agent, as for any session a host
  materializes after a restart.

- `meerkat-mob`: role-target admission and each step's choice of targets are
  checks that the mob actor and the flow engine make over the mob machine's
  member facts; the mob machine does not decide them itself. The role-wide
  target choice every flow step already used works the same way. The 0.9.6
  line moves both into the mob machine.

- `rkat-rpc`: a session subscription that overflowed reports its gap (the
  `stream_lagged` marker, and a typed SDK error when the stream ends with the
  gap open) but does not refill it. Take a run's token accounting from its
  run result, not from the streamed events.

- `meerkat-rpc`, `meerkat-mob`: a channel-scoped `execution_identity`
  (gpt-live-1) is served for a mob member local to the JSON-RPC server only.
  A placed member refuses it typed (`BridgeCommandRejected` with cause
  `Unsupported`, nothing dispatched to its host): the supervisor bridge does
  not carry an execution identity, and a member host started by
  `rkat mob host` serves WebSocket only. The 0.9.6 line extends the bridge.

- `meerkat`, `meerkat-runtime`: when lifecycle disposal itself closes a
  channel opened under a channel-scoped `execution_identity` (gpt-live-1),
  it closes it without the execution-identity authority's physical close and
  unbind, so the authority's transport can keep that channel's binding. That
  happens when such a channel is still open as its session is archived or
  destroyed: a session-scoped channel, or a mob member's channel whose
  session is disposed outside its mob. The mob's own close, retire, destroy,
  stop and shutdown close the channel through the authority first. Close the
  channel (`live/close` or `mob/member_live_close`) before disposing of its
  session. The 0.9.6 line runs the authority's close ahead of disposal.

## [0.9.4] - 2026-10-20

### Breaking

- `meerkat`: `session_runtime::live_orchestration::RealtimeSessionOpenProjectionError`
  gains the variant `Backpressured`: a live open refused because another
  live open on the host still holds the process's open-projection admission
  (see Fixed). Code that matches the enum exhaustively adds an arm for it.
- `meerkat-mob`: `SqliteMobObserverDrainReport` gains the field
  `retained_registrations: usize`: notification registrations of the
  drained observer's change watches that were still running when the drain
  stopped them (see Fixed). Code that builds the report with a struct
  literal sets it.
- `meerkat-mob`: `MemberRuntimeBuildIdentity` is no longer `UnwindSafe` or
  `RefUnwindSafe`: it now carries the member's exact
  `RuntimeSessionRegistrationWitness` (see `registration()` under Added),
  which is neither. A host that moves an identity into `catch_unwind` wraps
  it in `std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe`.
- Not measured by the gate (a behaviour change): `meerkat-mob`:
  `MobHandle::stop` no longer cancels its members' checkpoint saves, and
  neither does a failed `MobHandle::reset`: a run in flight at the Stop can
  still commit. A host that deletes a mob's storage after a Stop must
  Destroy the mob instead (see Fixed).
- Not measured by the gate (a parameter type change): `meerkat-runtime`:
  `ConfiguredMcpAttachmentProvider::configured` and
  `NativeWorkAuthorizationHost::configured_mcp_attachment_for_agent` take the
  session's exact `RuntimeSessionRegistrationWitness` instead of its
  `SessionId`, so a provider decides for one exact registration, not for
  whichever registration of that session asks. Read the id with
  `registration.session_id()`; a closure provider is
  `Fn(&RuntimeSessionRegistrationWitness, SessionAgentBinding) -> Option<..>`.
- `SessionAgentMandate::new` drops its `catalog` argument: it is now
  `new(executor, servers, represented_subject)`. `SessionAgentMandate::catalog_lineage`
  and the stock realm's `AgentGrantRefs::catalog_lineage` are removed. Nothing
  read the mandate's catalog lineage: the agent's tool catalog is base work,
  whose lineage the work's authority basis selects
  (`AgentGrantRefs::prompt_selection` still places the catalog grant there). A
  mandate now selects at least one MCP server (`AgentMandateError::NoSelection`
  otherwise, whose message now says so). A stock selection that grants only
  the catalog therefore binds no session agent: every configured MCP server
  stays unavailable, as before, and the registration's binding stays free for
  a server mandate.
- Stored input state is now version 7, assigned by the generated persistence
  version authority. A 0.9.4 binary writes every input row it stores at
  version 7, including a row it read at an older one; it still reads rows at
  versions 3 to 6 (0.9.0 to 0.9.3 wrote version 6). A 0.9.3 or older binary
  refuses a version 7 row before installing state and leaves the stored
  bytes in place, so there is no downgrade to 0.9.3 once a 0.9.4 binary has
  written any input row. Upgrade every process that shares a runtime store
  together.
- `meerkat-machine-schema`: a new public field on an exhaustively
  constructible struct (struct literals need it):
  `SessionPersistenceVersionAuthorityMachineState` gains
  `stored_input_state_migration_v6`.
- `meerkat-authorization-contracts`: `ExecutionRestrictions.resource_domains`
  is a `DomainRestriction` (it was `ExactRestriction<ResourceDomain>`). Build
  it with `DomainRestriction::{unrestricted, exact, owned_by, unresolved}` and
  read it through `DomainRestriction::bound`, which returns the
  `#[non_exhaustive]` `DomainBound` (`Unrestricted`, `Exact`, `OwnedBy`). A
  reader that cannot interpret a bound kind must treat it as naming nothing.
  Unrestricted and exact bounds keep the earlier wire bytes in both
  directions. A 0.9.3 binary refuses to restore a grant owner whose journal
  holds an owner-scoped restriction (`RestartRequired`); a journal that holds
  none stays readable by 0.9.3. An input row that carries an owner-scoped
  restriction is written at stored input state 7 (below); a row stamped before
  7 that carries one is rejected.
- Behaviour-only (not measured by the gate): `meerkat`:
  `StockGovernance::bind_prompt` binds only a prompt of the local operator
  (`Input::Prompt`). Any other input, an external event included, is
  refused with `StockGovernanceError::RequesterUnsupported` before anything
  is written: no candidate original and no change to the session's
  destination binding. 0.9.3 bound any input with the operator as its
  requester. Migration: a host whose one `bind_prompt` call served both the
  operator's prompts and an administrative outcome its own process reports
  (for example a connector finalization submitted as an external event of
  `InputOrigin::External` origin) keeps `bind_prompt` for the prompts and
  binds the outcome, as a durable event, with
  `StockGovernance::bind_host_outcome`; the reserved submission, the exact
  retained input and the rule that an uncertain delivery is resubmitted,
  never bound again, are unchanged.
- Behaviour-only (not measured by the gate): `meerkat`: a
  host-authenticated stock composition refuses its own stock ingress
  principal (`StockPrincipals::ingress_actor`) as a requester, with a Denied
  verdict before the host is asked, as it already refused the operator.
  0.9.3 asked the host about a caller equal to that principal, and could
  admit it.
- `meerkat-mob`: `MobError` is now `#[non_exhaustive]`, and gains the variant
  `MobError::ShutdownInProgress { mob_id }`, appended last (see the next
  entry). A downstream exhaustive `match` on `MobError` needs a wildcard arm.
- Behaviour-only (not measured by the gate): an admitted `MobHandle::shutdown`
  or `MobHandle::shutdown_with_report` closes the mob's admission before its
  teardown (see Fixed). From the Shutdown's admission (while it drains its own
  work, and while it is parked on its members' stops or on its runtime
  teardown), a command the Closing state refuses is refused with
  `MobError::AdmissionClosed` (reason `MobAdmissionCloseReason::Shutdown`): a
  spawn, respawn, work submission or flow run got
  `MobError::ActorCommandChannelClosed` there; while the Shutdown drained, so
  did the other refused commands (for example wiring, a host bind, a live
  commit, resume, reset or reload), which waited for the Shutdown or ran while
  it was parked. `MobHandle::acquire_owner` after the Shutdown's admission is
  refused the same way where it granted an owner lease. Every other request
  the actor answers while the Shutdown drains (a Stop, Destroy, Complete or
  retirement, a read, a status probe, `MobHandle::status` included) gets the
  new `MobError::ShutdownInProgress`, where v0.9.3 answered
  `MobError::ActorCommandChannelClosed`: retryable with the authority
  retained (wire code `SessionBusy`), returned by `MobHandle::stop` at once.
  Requests on the actor's internal lane, sent by the tasks the drain joins,
  keep `ActorCommandChannelClosed`, which otherwise now means the actor has
  exited or is exiting.
- Behaviour-only (not measured by the gate): a Shutdown that fails after its
  admission keeps the actor alive as the retry owner with admission closed,
  so the Closing set (spawn, work submission, flows, wiring, a host bind, a
  live commit, resume, reset, reload, owner leases and identity realization)
  stays refused with `MobError::AdmissionClosed` for the actor's life, where
  the actor admitted all of it again before. Stop, Shutdown and Destroy stay
  available.
- Behaviour-only (not measured by the gate): once a destroy is admitted (its
  durable destroy marker is written), `MobHandle::acquire_owner` is refused
  with `MobError::AdmissionClosed` (reason
  `MobAdmissionCloseReason::Destroyed`) where it granted an owner lease, and a
  command the Closing state refuses gets that error before the destroyed
  mob's own refusal (see Fixed). A mob restored with that marker starts
  closed: `MobBuilder::resume` returns its handle with admission already
  closed.
- Behaviour-only (not measured by the gate): after a durability fail-stop,
  `MobHandle::acquire_owner` is refused with `MobError::AdmissionClosed`
  (reason `MobAdmissionCloseReason::DurabilityFailStop`) where it granted an
  owner lease on the exited actor (see Fixed).
- Behaviour-only (not measured by the gate): after the mob's actor task is
  lost (it ends without its loop returning, as on a panic),
  `MobHandle::acquire_owner` is refused with `MobError::AdmissionClosed`
  (reason `MobAdmissionCloseReason::ActorLost`) where it granted an owner
  lease (see Fixed).
- Behaviour-only (not measured by the gate): after a composition dispatch
  failure stops the mob's actor, `MobHandle::acquire_owner` is refused with
  `MobError::AdmissionClosed` (reason
  `MobAdmissionCloseReason::DispatchFailed`) where it granted an owner lease
  on the stopped actor (see Fixed).
- Behaviour-only (not measured by the gate): `meerkat-skills` parses SKILL.md
  frontmatter with serde-saphyr 2.0 (pure Rust, no `unsafe`) instead of
  serde_yaml 0.9, and refuses frontmatter serde_yaml accepted:
  - a key given twice, at any level: a top-level extension key (however it
    is spelled) or a metadata key, where serde_yaml kept the last value. A
    duplicated known field or key inside a structured value was refused
    already;
  - a null (`~` or an empty value) as the `description` or a `metadata`
    value, which serde_yaml stored as the text `~` or an empty string;
  - an unrecognized tag (`!custom`) anywhere: on a typed field (`name`,
    `description`, `version`, a `metadata` value, a capability) serde_yaml
    dropped the tag and kept the value; on an extension value it was refused
    already;
  - nesting deeper than 64 levels, or 100 or more aliases that outnumber
    their anchors more than ten to one: the parser's default budget;
  - a `...` document end marker line, because serde-saphyr 2.0.0 ignores
    whatever follows one (malformed text included).

  A block scalar (`|`, `|+`, `>`) that ends the frontmatter now keeps its
  final line break, as YAML specifies and as it already did anywhere else in
  the frontmatter: the frontmatter was cut before that line break, so a
  `description: |` written last lost its trailing newline. Unchanged: YAML
  1.2 booleans (`yes`, `on` and `off` stay strings), `<<` as an ordinary key,
  and refusal of a second document. An alias expansion bomb is still
  refused; ordinary aliases now count against the budget above.
- MobMachine records each member identity's generation high-water across mob
  resets: `MobMachineState` (meerkat-machine-schema and meerkat-mob) and the
  kernel `State` (meerkat-machine-kernels) gain the fields
  `identity_generation_highwater` and `identity_generation_highwater_sealed`,
  so code that builds either struct literally must set them.
  `MobMachineSignal` (meerkat-machine-schema and meerkat-mob), its variant
  enum `MobMachineSignalVariant` (meerkat-machine-schema), and the kernel
  `Signal` and `SignalKind` gain the variants
  `RecoverIdentityGenerationHighwater` and `SealIdentityGenerationHighwater`,
  appended last. The kernel `generated::mob::TransitionId` gains
  `RecoverIdentityGenerationHighwaterRunning`,
  `RecoverIdentityGenerationHighwaterStopped`,
  `RecoverIdentityGenerationHighwaterCompleted`,
  `RecoverIdentityGenerationHighwaterDestroyed`,
  `SealIdentityGenerationHighwaterRunning`,
  `SealIdentityGenerationHighwaterStopped`,
  `SealIdentityGenerationHighwaterCompleted` and
  `SealIdentityGenerationHighwaterDestroyed`, also appended last, so no
  existing variant's discriminant moves. Exhaustive matches must add the
  arms.
- `meerkat-runtime`: `AuthenticatedOriginalSource::retained_original` is
  replaced by `retained_custody`, which returns `RetainedCustody`
  (`Retained`, `AdmissionPending` or `NotRetained`; non-exhaustive) instead of
  `Option<WorkAuthorityBasis>`. An implementor answers `AdmissionPending` only
  for a submission candidate that it will promote or withdraw itself, within
  its own bound; it withdraws any candidate it cannot settle, and a withdrawn
  candidate answers `NotRetained` from then on (see the method
  documentation). A candidate the implementor has not enrolled in such a
  settlement answers `NotRetained`, the earlier `None`.
- `meerkat`: `ContinuationAdmitError` gains `NotReady(ControllerReadinessFailure)`
  and is now `#[non_exhaustive]`. `retained_admission_outcome` maps a runtime
  that is not ready to admit a retained continuation, for a typed cause, to
  it: the continuation stays pending and is retried, as for `Failed`, and
  keeps the cause the runtime named.
- `meerkat`: `BlockedDeliveryReason` gains `NotReady(ControllerReadinessFailure)`,
  its first variant that carries data, so its variants no longer have defined
  discriminants. The drain blocks a continuation row the runtime is not ready
  to admit with it, and the delivery owner's pass failure line names the cause
  (for example `NotReady(OriginalAdmissionPending)`).
- `meerkat-contracts`: `WireControllerReadinessFailure` gains
  `OriginalAdmissionPending` (kind `original_admission_pending`), which
  `ControllerReadinessFailure::OriginalAdmissionPending` now maps to instead
  of `Unknown`. A Rust decoder of this type built before it rejects the new
  kind; the Python, TypeScript and Web SDKs keep error details as untyped
  data.
- `meerkat-llm-core`: `LlmDoneOutcome::Success` gains the field
  `stop_detail: Option<Box<ProviderStopDetail>>` (the provider's own account
  of a refusal or filter) and is `#[non_exhaustive]`: build it with
  `LlmDoneOutcome::success(stop_reason)` or
  `LlmDoneOutcome::success_with_detail(stop_reason, detail)`, and match it with
  `LlmDoneOutcome::Success { stop_reason, .. }`. The field is omitted from the
  serialized form when absent, so recorded frames keep their bytes.
- `meerkat-core`: `AgentError::ContentFiltered` gains the fields
  `stop: ContentFilteredStop` (`refusal` or `content_filter`, the refusing stop
  the provider ended on) and `detail: Option<Box<ProviderStopDetail>>`. A
  pattern that names `turn` without `..` needs the new fields.
- `meerkat-core`: `AgentErrorReason` gains the variant
  `ContentFiltered { stop, detail }`, appended last. The enum is exhaustive,
  so a `match` on it needs the new arm. Wire change: every
  content-filtered run failure now carries it, so `error_report.reason` of a
  `run_failed` event with class `content_filtered` goes from `null` to
  `{"reason_type": "content_filtered", "stop": ..., "detail": ...}` (`detail`
  omitted when the provider sent none). SDKs of earlier versions read it as an
  unknown reason and keep it raw. Downgrade: the session event store decodes
  every line strictly, so a 0.9.3 binary cannot read a session event log that
  holds such a `run_failed` line.
- `meerkat-core`: a compaction summary reports what its source carried.
  `Compactor::prepare_for_summarization` takes the summarization source budget
  and returns the source with its bound, `(messages: &[Message], budget:
  Option<SummarizationSourceBudget>) -> SummarizationSource`, and has no
  default implementation: every compactor states how it bounds the transcript
  it sends to the model that writes the summary. The budget is that model's
  (`SummarizationSourceBudget::for_summary_model`), `None` when the model
  declares no context window. `CompactionSummarySource` is `#[non_exhaustive]`
  and its `ProviderCall` variant carries the call's `source_bound`, and
  `AgentEvent::CompactionCompleted` and `CompactionProjectionIntent` gain
  `summary_source`, `None` only for one recorded before this release (on the
  wire the field is optional). A
  compactor that used the default keeps its old behaviour by returning
  `SummarizationSource::whole(meerkat_core::materialize_latest_system_prompt_versions(messages))`
  and ignoring the budget; to fit the summarizing model, it also bounds the
  result by the budget and reports the bound, as `DefaultCompactor` does. The
  implementors in this repository (`DefaultCompactor` and the test
  compactors) are updated; no published example implements the trait.
- `meerkat-core`: `Agent::replace_client` and
  `Agent::replace_client_with_request_policy`, and through them the ephemeral
  service's `SessionService::set_session_client`, no longer change the
  session's model. A client, or a request-policy model, whose provider or
  model differs from the session's durable identity is refused with
  `AgentError::ClientModelChangeRequiresHotSwap` before anything changes: such
  a swap left the durable identity and the active model profile, which size
  the context and compaction budgets, on the previous model. Change the model
  with `Agent::hot_swap_llm_identity` or
  `SessionService::hot_swap_session_llm_identity`, which publish the client,
  the durable identity and the profile together. A replacement client for the
  same model, or any client on a session without a durable identity, is
  accepted as before.
- `meerkat-core`: a compaction rewrite records the history it left.
  `SessionCompactionCadence` and `CompactionContext` gain
  `last_rewrite_history_tokens`, the estimated history tokens the last rewrite
  left (`None` before the first), which `Compactor::should_compact` reads; the
  session persists it with its compaction cadence.
  `AgentEvent::CompactionCompleted` and `CompactionProjectionIntent` gain
  `estimated_history_tokens_after`, the same estimate in the unit of
  `estimated_history_tokens`, `None` for one recorded before this release or
  when the history could not be measured (on the wire the field is optional;
  the Python SDK reads it as `CompactionCompleted.estimated_history_tokens_after`
  and the TypeScript SDK as
  `CompactionCompletedEvent.estimatedHistoryTokensAfter`). A
  `CompactionContext` built by hand keeps the previous decisions with
  `last_rewrite_history_tokens: None`. A 0.9.3 binary ignores the persisted
  field and drops it when it next writes the cadence; back on this release,
  that session compacts as before until its next rewrite records the field
  again, so a downgrade and upgrade cost at most one extra summary call.
- `meerkat-authorization-contracts`: `AuditObservation` is now
  `#[non_exhaustive]`, so a match outside the crate needs a wildcard arm.
  `AuditObservation::Refused` gains `read: Option<AuditRefusalRead>`
  (patterns without `..` and literals need it), and the exhaustively
  constructible `AuditPolicyRead` gains `publication_instance:
  Option<uuid::Uuid>` (struct literals need it).
- Child tool bundle opt-in (see Added):
  - `meerkat-mob-mcp`: `ChildToolBundleAvailability` gains `ChildOffered`
    and is now `#[non_exhaustive]`; `ChildMcpServerRegistrationError` gains
    `OfferNotSupported` and is now `#[non_exhaustive]`. A `match` over either
    needs a wildcard arm.
  - `meerkat-mob`: `ToolConfig` gains the field `bundles: Vec<String>`, and
    `MobError` gains the variant `ToolBundleNotOffered`. Code that builds a
    `ToolConfig` with a struct literal sets the field, or uses
    `..ToolConfig::default()`.
  - `meerkat-contracts`: `MobToolConfigInput` gains the field
    `bundles: Vec<String>` (the public `tools.bundles`). Code that builds it
    with a struct literal sets the field.
- `meerkat-core`, `meerkat-mcp`, wire and SDKs: the lifecycle bit of tool
  configuration changes is named `settled`, not `persisted` (#1658). It says
  whether a change is a settled lifecycle fact rather than a pending or
  draining step. It never said whether anything was written to
  configuration: that is the `persisted` of the `mcp/add`, `mcp/remove` and
  `mcp/reload` requests and responses, which keep their name and meaning.
  - Wire: `tool_config_changed` event payloads, stored `tool_config` notice
    payloads and `mcp` notice blocks that 0.9.4 builds carry `settled`
    instead of `persisted`. Rows and events stored by 0.9.3 and earlier keep
    the key and value they were stored with when they are read back, served
    in history or replayed, so their transcript digests, session heads and
    rewrite records still verify. Readers must accept either key; the
    schemas list both and require neither.
  - Readers derive the fact instead of trusting the stored bit:
    `ToolConfigChangedPayload::settled()` from `status_info`, and
    `SystemNoticeBlock::lifecycle_settled()` from an `mcp` block's `phase`
    (an `mcp` block without a phase reports its stored bit, `settled` or
    0.9.3's `persisted`). The tool-scope, deferred-catalog and failed-closed
    notices that 0.9.3 stored with `persisted: false` read as settled.
  - Rust API: `ToolConfigChangedPayload::new` takes no lifecycle argument
    (the status decides it), and the public `ToolConfigChangedPayload`
    field `persisted` is replaced by `ToolConfigChangedPayload::settled()`.
    The public `ExternalToolDelta` field `persisted` is removed in favour of
    `ExternalToolDelta::settled()`, derived from `phase` and not serialized.
    `SystemNoticeBlock::Mcp { persisted }` is now
    `SystemNoticeBlock::Mcp { lifecycle_bit }`, a `ToolConfigLifecycleBit`
    (`Settled`, `Persisted` or `Absent`) that keeps the stored spelling; read
    the fact through `SystemNoticeBlock::lifecycle_settled()`. `meerkat-mcp`'s
    `ExternalToolSurfaceEffect::EmitExternalToolDelta { persisted }` is now
    `{ settled }`. New: `ToolConfigLifecycleBit`,
    `ToolConfigChangedPayload::lifecycle_bit`,
    `SystemNoticeBlock::lifecycle_settled`,
    `ExternalToolDeltaPhase::is_settled` and
    `ToolConfigChangeStatus::is_settled`.
  - SDKs: the Python and TypeScript `ToolConfigChangedPayload.persisted` is
    now `settled`. Their event parsers derive it from `status_info` the way
    rkat-rpc does and use the stored bit (`settled`, or `persisted` from
    rkat-rpc 0.9.3 and earlier) only for a status they do not know. Stored
    notices in session history stay raw and carry either key. The generated
    Python, TypeScript and Web types follow the schemas, with both keys
    optional.
  - Version skew: the 0.9.3 Python and TypeScript SDKs require `persisted`,
    so a 0.9.3 SDK talking to a 0.9.4 rkat-rpc fails on every
    `tool_config_changed` event that 0.9.4 builds. An SDK downloads its own
    matching rkat-rpc only when it is given none, so this happens with a
    binary it is given: `MEERKAT_BIN_PATH`, an explicit path, or an rkat-rpc
    on `PATH` (a Homebrew upgrade, for example); the remedy is to upgrade the
    SDK.
  - Stored transcripts: 0.9.3 cannot read back a transcript that 0.9.4 wrote
    with a `tool_config` notice (a tool-scope, deferred-catalog or
    failed-closed notice), because 0.9.3 requires the payload's `persisted`.
    An `mcp` notice block reads back on 0.9.3 with `persisted: false`, which
    0.9.3 consults only for `McpPending` blocks, where 0.9.4 also writes
    `false`.
- Not measured by the gate (a return type change): `meerkat`:
  `RuntimeDeliveryOwnerRetirement::join` returns
  `Result<RuntimeDeliveryOwnerRetired, RuntimeDeliveryOwnerRetirementIncomplete>`
  instead of `Result<(), RuntimeDeliveryOwnerRetirementIncomplete>`: the
  report names the store watch's notification registration the retirement
  left with the process (see Added). The report is `#[must_use]`: code that
  uses `?` or otherwise discards it now gets an `unused_must_use` warning
  and binds or reads it; code that matches `Ok(())` matches `Ok(_)` or
  reads the report.
- `meerkat-machine-schema`, `meerkat-machine-kernels` and `meerkat-runtime`:
  the live delegation narration kind `LiveDelegationNarrationKind` gains
  `FinishedPending`, appended last, in the schema catalog's DSL enum, the
  kernels' generated copy and the runtime's copy
  (`meerkat_runtime::live_execution::LiveDelegationNarrationKind`). It is
  never spoken: the machine authorizes it for a delegation whose work has
  finished with an eligible result not yet handed to delivery (see Fixed).
  The enums are exhaustive, so a `match` on one adds the arm.
- `meerkat-live`: the provider adapter carrier `LiveSidebandProviderCommand`
  gains `NoteDelegationFinishedContext { binding, attempt, delegation }`,
  which only `LiveSidebandCommand::note_delegation_finished` produces, from
  the new one-shot `LiveSidebandFinishedNoticeAuthority`. A provider adapter
  that matches the carrier lowers or refuses it.
- `meerkat-openai`: `GptLiveBrokerObservation` gains
  `InstructionsContextAppendWithdrawn { token }`, appended last: a
  delegation's finished notice that waited while the model was speaking and
  was withdrawn unsent because a result of the delegation reached the session
  first (see Fixed). The enum is exhaustive, so a `match` on it adds the arm.
- `meerkat-llm-core`: `RealtimeSessionEvent` gains the variant
  `TurnFailed { response_id, failure, accounting }` (#1883). The enum is
  exhaustive, so a `match` over it needs the new arm.
- `meerkat-core`: `RealtimeTranscriptEvent` gains the variant
  `AssistantTurnFailed { response_id }` (#1883). The enum is exhaustive.
- `meerkat-machine-schema`, `meerkat-core` and `meerkat-machine-kernels`:
  `RealtimeTranscriptStopReasonKind` (the session document's DSL enum and
  its two generated copies) gains the variant `Failed`, appended after
  `Other` (#1883). All three are exhaustive.
- `meerkat-live`: `LiveProjectionSink` gains the required method
  `signal_turn_failed(session_id, response_id, failure, accounting)` (#1883).
  It has no default body: every sink decides what a failed response
  discards and records.
- Storage: a HeadCanonical session that records a failed realtime response
  writes realtime sidecar event schema 4 (#1883). Meerkat 0.9.3 and earlier
  refuse such a session with "unsupported realtime event schema 4", so a
  session cannot be opened by an older binary once a failed realtime response
  has been recorded in it.
- `meerkat-mob`: `MemberShutdownOutcome::UnregisterPending` carries
  `settlement: MemberUnregisterSettlement` and is `#[non_exhaustive]`: match
  it with `{ stage, .. }`. The settlement follows the exact registration's
  runtime unregister after Shutdown returns.
- Behaviour (no type change): every content steer admitted while a turn runs
  (a prompt, a peer message, request or lifecycle notice, an external event or
  a local flow step) is now written into the running turn's transcript at a
  model boundary (`MeerkatMachine` delivery class `DurableAppend`) or, when it
  carries something only a fresh turn applies or is a directed delivery,
  taken by exactly one follow-up turn. Before, peer message and request
  steers and text-only prompt steers reached exactly one model request and
  never the transcript. Hosts and consoles now see their rows in history,
  `boundary_append_applied` when the runner writes them, and one
  `peer_content_ingested` per incoming comms notice. Durable steers join one
  per boundary, in arrival order: a steer admitted while an earlier one still
  waits joins the boundary after it, in the same run, instead of falling back
  to the follow-up turn; steers still waiting when the run ends take the
  follow-up turn in arrival order. Before, every peer or text steer admitted
  during one boundary reached the next model request; now one durable steer
  joins per boundary, and the later ones land at later boundaries of the run
  or in the follow-up turn.
- `meerkat-core`: `SystemNoticeBlock::Comms` and
  `AgentEvent::PeerContentIngested` gain the field
  `delivery_id: Option<InteractionId>`: the delivery id of an incoming peer
  message, which `reply_to_peer` takes as `reply_to` (see Fixed). Struct
  literals and exhaustive patterns of either variant name it. On the wire it
  is optional (`delivery_id` on the notice block and on
  `peer_content_ingested`) and omitted when absent.
- `meerkat-core`: `CommsCommand::PeerMessage`, `InteractionContent::Message`
  and `SystemNoticeBlock::Comms` gain `in_reply_to: Option<InteractionId>`;
  `meerkat-comms`: `MessageKind::Message` gains `in_reply_to: Option<Uuid>`;
  `meerkat-runtime`: `PeerInput` gains `in_reply_to`. It is the delivery a
  `reply_to_peer` reply answers (see Added). Struct literals and exhaustive
  patterns name it. On the wire it is optional (`in_reply_to` on the notice
  block) and omitted when absent.
- Behaviour (no type change): the text the model reads for an incoming peer
  message notice now carries a `Delivery ID: <id>` line after its payload, and
  an `In reply to: <id>` line when the message is a reply.
- Compatibility (not measured by the gate): the transcript content digest
  erases a comms notice's `delivery_id` and `in_reply_to`, as it erases a
  notice's runtime origin, so a row's revision is the same with or without
  them. A 0.9.3 reader, which drops the keys when it decodes the row, computes
  the revision 0.9.4 stored and loads the session. One residual: an append
